kernel/rng-shared-stream.title: Shared env.rng stream makes outputs depend on cook history and node key order
kernel/rng-shared-stream.evidence: GraphEnv.rng (types.ts:204) is one stream that every rng operator draws from in topo order. Probe: a graph with two circle-pack nodes a and b, env rng new SeededRNG(42). A full cook gives b positions 872.9,573.0,... Then setParams({'b.margin':110}), cook, setParams({'b.margin':100}), cook: b's output becomes 331.9,266.5,..., which is identical to a's output and differs from the original full cook. Listing the nodes as {b, a} instead of {a, b} also swaps the outputs (Kahn's FIFO queue at graph.ts:130-143 follows Object.keys order). A seed change (cook with SeededRNG(42), then SeededRNG(7)) re-cooks 0 nodes, because rng is not a $env wire (cook.ts:169-177). Operators fall back silently to Math.random when env.rng is missing (circle-pack.ts:50, poisson-disc.ts:114, dash-stroke.ts:16, binary-subdivide.ts:54). frame.tsx:141 hides the problem by creating a fresh SeededRNG(42) per cook and clearing the whole cache after every draw; editor-preview.tsx:66 does not clear the cache, so its incremental re-cooks show wrong output. rng.ts:43 fork() mixes in this.d, a counter that advances on every draw, so fork is not a pure function of (seed, tag). From my own knowledge, not checked against sources here: Meridian and Subscapes are hash-seeded Art Blocks-style works, where the same seed must produce the same image, so this breaks the project's core goal.
kernel/rng-shared-stream.recommendation: Make the kernel own seeding: give each node an RNG built from (graph seed, node key, optional per-node seed param), with the graph seed as a declared, diffed input. Remove the Math.random fallbacks, make fork a pure function of (construction seed, tag), and add tests showing that a full cook equals an incremental cook and that node key order does not change outputs.
kernel/rng-shared-stream.verifyNote: Re-ran the probe in bun 1.3.9 against the worktree (scratch script under $TMPDIR). Two circle-pack nodes {a,b} with a fresh SeededRNG(42): a full cook gives a=331.9,266.5 and b=872.9,573.0. After setParams b.margin 110 then back to 100, b re-cooks alone (cooked=1) and becomes 331.9,266.5, the same as a. Listing {b,a} swaps the outputs. Cooking with SeededRNG(7) after SeededRNG(42) re-cooks 0 nodes. fork: r.fork('x').random() gives 0.2279; after one r.random() the same call gives 0.9067, so fork depends on draw count (rng.ts:43 XORs this.d, which counts up at rng.ts:37). The Math.random fallbacks are at circle-pack.ts:50, poisson-disc.ts:114, binary-subdivide.ts:54 and dash-stroke.ts:16. frame.tsx:141 builds a fresh SeededRNG(42) and calls clearCache at :163. editor-preview.tsx:66 builds a fresh RNG but never clears the cache, so after any stroke-param edit in the editor, dash-stroke in flowFieldGraph re-cooks from the start of the stream instead of after circle-pack's 6000 draws. That is visible in a shipped host.

kernel/implicit-env-reads.title: Env values read directly by operators (dpr, rng, _gl, createCanvas) bypass dirty tracking
kernel/implicit-env-reads.evidence: CookEngine diffs only env keys that appear as $env wire outputs (envDependents, cook.ts:86-94 and 169-177). Operators also read env directly: dpr at stroke-renderer.ts:58, point-renderer.ts:32 and field-render.ts:74; _gl at field-render.ts:20; createCanvas at several sites. No patch wires $env.dpr (grep found no output:"dpr" wire). Probe: a fake op returning env.dpr, cooked with {dpr:1} then {dpr:2}, evaluated once and kept output 1. GraphEnv is `Record<string, unknown> & {createCanvas?, rng?}` (types.ts:201-205), so operators cast, as in `((env as GraphEnv | undefined)?.dpr as number) ?? 1`. The only reason this goes unnoticed in Frame is frame.tsx clearing the cache on every draw.
kernel/implicit-env-reads.recommendation: Split GraphEnv into declared, typed values that the engine diffs (width, height, dpr, seed, later time), with each operator declaring which ones it reads, and a separate capability context (canvas factory, GL) that is never diffed. Remove the casts and fix the cook() doc comment.
kernel/implicit-env-reads.verifyNote: envDependents is built only from $env wires (cook.ts:86-94) and diffed at cook.ts:169-177. Across all 14 shipped graphs the only $env outputs wired are width and height (97 height and 30 width wires). The cook() doc comment at cook.ts:158 says it diffs 'width, height, dpr', which is false unless someone wires dpr. Operators read dpr directly at stroke-renderer.ts:58, point-renderer.ts:32 and field-render.ts:74, and _gl at field-render.ts:20, each through an `as` cast. Today the dpr part is masked: Frame clears its cache every draw and EditorPreview fixes dpr at 1. rng is the observable case of the same root cause, so this overlaps rng-shared-stream. It still blocks a sound incremental engine.

kernel/mutable-cache-no-lifecycle.title: Cached outputs are shared mutable references with no resource lifecycle; operators and the host work around it
kernel/mutable-cache-no-lifecycle.evidence: cook.ts:234-237 stores the evaluate result by reference and passes the same objects downstream. Nothing freezes or owns them. composite.ts:66 and :73 run `layers[i]._canvas = undefined` on its inputs, which are the upstream stroke-renderers' cached Buffer2D objects, to free GPU memory (comment at stroke-renderer.ts:343-353). If composite re-cooks while its inputs stay clean (for example after a change to its 'mode' param), the layers no longer carry _canvas, so it takes the CPU blend path (composite.ts:99) instead of the drawImage path: output depends on cook history. The cache has no budget or eviction, so the host clears everything: frame.tsx calls engine.clearCache() after every draw (comment: '~100 MB per panel at 2x DPR, crashing the tab'), and cook.ts:282-292 documents the same. Incremental cooking is therefore turned off in the main renderer.
kernel/mutable-cache-no-lifecycle.recommendation: Make immutable outputs a kernel invariant (freeze in dev, plus a test). Give resources an explicit owner with a lifecycle: an optional Operator.dispose(output) or disposable values released on eviction, plus a retention policy. Stop operators and hosts from writing to inputs, including blitBuffer2D. See also the missed finding on Buffer2D's Float32 storage, the main reason memory blows up.
kernel/mutable-cache-no-lifecycle.verifyNote: cook.ts:234-237 stores evaluate results by reference. composite.ts:66/:73 null out `_canvas` on its input layers, which are the upstream cached outputs. A later re-cook of composite alone (for example a 'mode' change in EditorPreview, which never clears its cache) then falls to the CPU blend at composite.ts:99. That blend uses non-premultiplied math on quantized readback, so it can differ from drawImage/globalCompositeOperation. The reader missed two more mutation sites. The host's blitBuffer2D (render/canvas-2d.ts:136-139) also sets `buffer._canvas = undefined` on the cached terminal output. composite.ts:50 returns the upstream object itself when there is one layer, which aliases two cache entries. The comments at frame.tsx:159-163 and cook.ts:282-292 confirm clearCache-after-draw is a memory workaround that turns incremental cooking off in Frame.

kernel/missing-graph-invariants.title: CookEngine never validates the graph; $env, outputs, node keys and shader-only ops go unchecked
kernel/missing-graph-invariants.evidence: The CookEngine constructor calls topoSort only (cook.ts:69), and validateGraph is never called anywhere in packages/ or apps/ (grep). topoSort crashes with a TypeError on a wire to an unknown node. Probe: topoSort(['x'], [{from:'x',to:'ghost'}]) throws "undefined is not an object (evaluating 'downstream.get(key)')" (graph.ts:139), and an unknown source throws at graph.ts:127. validateGraph skips type checks for $env wires (graph.ts:73). Probe: $env.width wired into merge.geometry passes validation. It also does not check for cycles. Evaluate results are cast without checking (cook.ts:236). Probe: an op returning {wrong:1} gives its downstream {n: undefined}, silently. An op without evaluate is skipped (cook.ts:194), leaves no cache entry, is counted as 'cached' in stats (cook.ts:242), and its consumers receive undefined. Probe: stats {cooked:1, cached:1}, sink got {n: undefined}. Node keys are not validated: setParams splits on the first '.' (cook.ts:139), so a key containing '.' or a node named '$env' misbehaves. cook() returns the internal mutable cache Map (cook.ts:245).
kernel/missing-graph-invariants.recommendation: Add a validate step in the CookEngine constructor (or CookEngine.create) that runs validateGraph, declares $env's outputs and their types, rejects node keys containing '.' or starting with '$', and reports cycles with node names. In dev, check that evaluate returns every declared output key and that each referenced op exists. Return a read-only view of the cache.
kernel/missing-graph-invariants.verifyNote: Confirmed: the constructor calls only topoSort (cook.ts:69), and validateGraph is referenced only by the index.ts re-export. topoSort with a wire to a ghost node throws "undefined is not an object (evaluating 'downstream.get(key)')" at graph.ts:139, and a ghost source throws at graph.ts:127. A $env.width wire into merge.geometry passes validateGraph (the source check is skipped at graph.ts:73). A no-evaluate op gives stats {cooked:1, cached:1} and its sink gets {n: undefined}. Node key 'a.b' with setParams({'a.b.k':1}) dirties a nonexistent node 'a' (needsCook=true), and 'a.b' keeps its old value after cook. cook() returns the internal Map (cook.ts:245). An unknown op type is also only found mid-cook (cook.ts:193), after earlier nodes have cooked. Useful fact: all 14 shipped graphs pass validateGraph today (probe), so running it in the constructor costs nothing. A related symptom of $env's undeclared outputs: editor/types.ts:59-63 inferEnvPortType returns 'number' on both branches.

kernel/setparams-aliasing.title: setParams keeps the caller's object, so in-place edits are never detected; params are not validated
kernel/setparams-aliasing.evidence: cook.ts:150 `this.prevParams = params;` stores the reference. Probe: p = {'a.margin':100}; setParams(p); cook; then p['a.margin'] = 300; setParams(p); cook re-cooks 0 nodes and vertexCount stays 198. Also from probe: setParams({'a.nope':1, 'a.margin':99999, 'zzz.margin':3, 'nodot':1}) is accepted. Unknown keys, out-of-range values and unknown nodes are not rejected, and 'zzz' is added to the dirty set (propagate at cook.ts:141 does not check membership), so needsCook reports true spuriously.
kernel/setparams-aliasing.recommendation: Copy params in setParams ({...params}). In dev, reject keys whose node or param does not exist (checked against collectParams). Add clamp flags to ParamDef instead of treating min/max as hard limits. Index external params by node once (the main checkout's uncommitted _buildParamIndex already does this).
kernel/setparams-aliasing.verifyNote: The mechanics are right. cook.ts:150 keeps the caller's object. Editing p in place and calling setParams(p) re-cooks 0 nodes (sink stays 1). setParams({'a.k':5,'zzz.k':3}) leaves needsCook=true for a node that does not exist. But no current caller can hit the aliasing: frame.tsx:54 updates values immutably with a spread, and EditorPreview receives entry.values from React state. The suggestion to 'clamp or reject values outside min/max' is wrong for this model. min/max here are slider ranges, as in TouchDesigner where (from my knowledge) normMin/normMax set the slider and clamping is a separate per-parameter flag. Clamping by default would silently change patches.

kernel/kernel-dom-coupling.title: Kernel types carry browser/GPU types (OffscreenCanvas; WebGL in the uncommitted work)
kernel/kernel-dom-coupling.evidence: types.ts:96 has `_canvas?: OffscreenCanvas` on Buffer2D, the universal TOP currency. types.ts:202 has `createCanvas?: (w, h) => OffscreenCanvas` on GraphEnv. The doc comment at types.ts:84-89 describes a lazy `data` getter, but only composite.ts:82 implements one. packages/engine/tsconfig.json gives the whole package lib ["ES2022","DOM"], so nothing stops DOM types entering the kernel. The kernel runs headless at runtime (probe), but cannot compile without DOM. The main checkout's uncommitted diff adds a GPUBuffer2D class (WebGL2RenderingContext, WebGLTexture, WebGLFramebuffer, gl.readPixels) to kernel/types.ts and imports it into kernel/cook.ts, which deepens the coupling.
kernel/kernel-dom-coupling.recommendation: Keep the kernel backend-agnostic: use an opaque or generic backing handle on Buffer2D owned by render/, put canvas and WebGL types in render/, and give kernel/ its own tsconfig with lib ES2022 only so the compiler enforces the boundary. Apply the same rule when porting GPUBuffer2D from the uncommitted work.
kernel/kernel-dom-coupling.verifyNote: Compiling only kernel/{cook,graph,registry,rng,types}.ts with lib es2022 and types node fails with exactly two errors: types.ts(96,13) and types.ts(202,44), both 'Cannot find name OffscreenCanvas'. packages/engine/tsconfig.json adds DOM to lib for the whole package. The main checkout's uncommitted diff (read only) adds a GPUBuffer2D class with WebGL2RenderingContext/WebGLTexture/readPixels to kernel/types.ts, and `import { GPUBuffer2D } from "./types"` to kernel/cook.ts, as the reader said.

kernel/kernel-imports-operators.title: The kernel depends on operator implementations (an import cycle via noise)
kernel/kernel-imports-operators.evidence: field-expr.ts:1-2 imports pnoise from ../operators/top/perlin-noise and simplex2 from ../operators/top/simplex-noise. Those files import createField and the builders back from ../../kernel/field-expr (perlin-noise.ts:3, simplex-noise.ts:3), which is a circular import. It works only because ESM bindings are live and the uses sit inside functions. The noise primitives already share noise-utils.ts (the P table) at the src root. Operators also reach into the render layer: field-render.ts:4 and grid-sampler.ts:4 import render/webgl.
kernel/kernel-imports-operators.recommendation: Move pnoise, simplex2 and P into one noise module below both kernel and operators. Enforce the direction 'operators import kernel, never the reverse' (a lint rule or separate tsconfig). Inject render backends through the capability context.
kernel/kernel-imports-operators.verifyNote: field-expr.ts:1-2 imports pnoise and simplex2 from operators/top/*. perlin-noise.ts:3 and simplex-noise.ts:3 import createField, X, Y and the builders back from kernel/field-expr. It is a real cycle. It survives because X and Y (field-expr.ts:184-185, const) are only touched inside evaluate. If either noise module ever uses them at top level, that becomes a TDZ error. These are the only kernel imports that leave kernel/ (grep). field-render.ts:4 and grid-sampler.ts:4 import render/webgl.

kernel/port-types-too-coarse.title: Port types cannot express geometry dimension; 'signal' is unused and 'number' wires come only from $env
kernel/port-types-too-coarse.evidence: PortType (types.ts:25-33) has a single 'geometry' covering both Geometry<2> and Geometry<3>. surface-lift.ts:4 outputs Geometry<3> while stroke-renderer.ts:3 expects Geometry<2>. validateGraph's string-equality check (graph.ts:85) accepts a surface-lift → stroke-renderer wire, which would render garbage. 'signal' appears on no port (grep of type: "signal" finds 0). 25 ports are type 'number', fed only by $env wires whose types are never declared or checked.
kernel/port-types-too-coarse.recommendation: Encode dimension in the port type (geometry2/geometry3, or a {kind, dim} descriptor) and check it in validateGraph. Meanwhile make the 3D operators stride by geometry.dim or assert dim===3. Declare $env output types and drop 'signal' until CHOPs exist.
kernel/port-types-too-coarse.verifyNote: The core claim holds: a single 'geometry' PortType covers both Geometry<2> and Geometry<3>, 25 ports are type 'number', and 0 ports are 'signal'. But the example points the wrong way. A surface-lift (Geometry<3>) → stroke-renderer wire does not 'render garbage': stroke-renderer strides by geometry.dim (stroke-renderer.ts:108, 131-153), and so does point-renderer (:67-71), so a 3D input renders as an XY top-down projection with Z dropped. Garbage comes from the other direction: 2D geometry into project-3d (project-3d.ts:37-39) or geometric-normal (geometric-normal.ts:42-44), which hard-code stride 3 and ignore dim.

kernel/operator-type-erasure.title: The Operator generic defaults to any; evaluate params are untyped, which causes 114 duplicated defaults
kernel/operator-type-erasure.evidence: types.ts:221 declares `Operator<TInputs = any, TOutputs = any>`. allOperators: Operator[] (index.ts:112) and the registry Map<string, Operator> (registry.ts:4) erase every operator's Inputs and Outputs. CookEngine passes Record<string, unknown>, where unwired or missing inputs are undefined, while the operator's Inputs type says the field is required. params is Record<string, number> (types.ts:235), so operators write `params.x ?? literal`: 114 times in 33 files (probe), restating declared defaults. In camera-3d the restated values are wrong (fallback eyeX 300 vs declared 0.75, orthoSize 500 vs 1.25; camera-3d.ts:216, 224, 246, 264). One `as any` sits at types.ts:332.
kernel/operator-type-erasure.recommendation: Add defineOperator() with const generics that derives Inputs from PortDefs (optional → T | undefined, variadic → T[], and have the kernel pass [] for unwired variadics) and params from ParamDef keys. Delete the `??` fallbacks. Erase the types only at the registry boundary.
kernel/operator-type-erasure.verifyNote: types.ts:221 Operator<TInputs = any, TOutputs = any>; allOperators: Operator[] (index.ts:112); registry Map<string, Operator> (registry.ts:4); `as any` at types.ts:332. The regex `params\.\w+ \?\?` finds 110 fallbacks in 33 files (the reader said 114; close). camera-3d's fallbacks (eyeX 300 vs default 0.75 at :216/:246; orthoSize 500 vs 1.25 at :224/:264) are wrong but unreachable through CookEngine, because cook.ts:224 always fills every declared default first. So they are misleading dead code, not a live bug. Unwired optional and variadic inputs arrive as undefined rather than [] (cook.ts:203-220), which the Inputs types do not express.

kernel/cook-failure-handling.title: One throwing operator aborts the whole cook and leaves stats stale; there is no per-node error state
kernel/cook-failure-handling.evidence: cook.ts:233-239 has no try/catch. Probe: in a graph src→bad where bad throws, cook() rethrows 'boom', src is cached, needsCook stays true, and stats.cooked shows 0 from the previous call. Frame's draw() (frame.tsx ~128-170) does not catch, so one bad parameter value blanks the panel. From my own knowledge: TouchDesigner flags the failing operator with an error and keeps cooking independent branches.
kernel/cook-failure-handling.recommendation: Catch errors per node, store {error} for that node, skip and mark its descendants, cook unrelated branches, and report errors in CookStats for the editor.
kernel/cook-failure-handling.verifyNote: No try/catch around cook.ts:233-239. In the src→bad probe, cook rethrows 'boom', src stays cached and needsCook stays true. A stronger probe: a headless cook of subscapesTerrain3dGraph throws at the first stroke-renderer in topo order, and normals/cull/proj/shade, which do not depend on that node, are never cooked (19/27 nodes cached). So one failure also starves independent branches. frame.tsx draw() (128-171) has no catch. From my own knowledge, TouchDesigner flags the erroring operator and keeps cooking unaffected nodes.

kernel/push-cook-terminal-heuristic.title: cook() evaluates every dirty node; the viewed output is chosen by a first-terminal-of-type heuristic
kernel/push-cook-terminal-heuristic.evidence: cook.ts:189-240 walks the full topo order and evaluates every dirty node, whether or not it feeds the output being displayed. findTerminalOutput (cook.ts:261-275) returns the first node with no consumers whose output port matches the type, iterating terminalKeys in topo order, so with two terminal buffers the choice depends on node key order. A node that has consumers can never be viewed. graph.ts:181-217 reimplements the same lookup as free functions, used nowhere outside the index re-export. From my own knowledge: TouchDesigner cooks on demand, pulling from viewers and output operators, and marks the viewed node with display and render flags.
kernel/push-cook-terminal-heuristic.recommendation: Add cook(targets) that evaluates only the dirty ancestors of the requested outputs. Store an explicit display or output designation on the Graph. Delete the graph.ts terminal helpers. Do this together with the editor work, not before.
kernel/push-cook-terminal-heuristic.verifyNote: cook() does walk every dirty node (cook.ts:189-240), and findTerminalOutput iterates terminalKeys in topo order (cook.ts:261-275). The graph.ts:178-217 duplicates are unused outside the index re-export. But all 14 shipped graphs have exactly one terminal (probe). With one terminal in a DAG every node feeds it, so push and pull cook the same set today, and the 'first terminal' choice is never ambiguous. 'A node that has consumers can never be viewed' is wrong at the API level: getOutput(nodeKey) exists (cook.ts:256). Only the hosts limit themselves to findTerminalOutput. The gap is real for the node editor (viewing intermediate nodes, several terminals), not for current patches.

kernel/no-time-model.title: No time or frame in the environment and no time-dependent operators; the CHOP family is empty
kernel/no-time-model.evidence: GraphEnv (types.ts:201-205) has no time or frame field. Operator has no time-dependence flag. The dirty sources (cook.ts:135-177, 278-296) are only params and $env diffs. operators/chop/index.ts is a two-line placeholder comment, and Signal (types.ts:147) and the 'signal' port type are unused. From my own knowledge: TouchDesigner's cook loop is driven by the timeline (absTime and frame), time-dependent operators re-cook every frame, and CHOPs carry animated channels that drive parameters.
kernel/no-time-model.recommendation: When animation is needed, add time and frame as declared env inputs, and mark timeDependent operators (or derive it from a time read) so the engine dirties them each tick. Design this together with parameter bindings.
kernel/no-time-model.verifyNote: GraphEnv (types.ts:201-205) has no time or frame. The only dirty sources are params and the $env diff. chop/index.ts is a two-line comment. Signal and 'signal' are unused. Severity lowered: Meridian and Subscapes are static, hash-seeded images (from my own knowledge), so nothing in the current reverse-engineering goal needs a timeline. It matters for TouchDesigner fidelity later.

kernel/params-model.title: Parameters are numeric constants only: no toggle, string, vector or colour types and no expressions or bindings
kernel/params-model.evidence: ParamDef = NumericParamDef | EnumParamDef (types.ts:47-68), and enum option values are numbers. NodeInstance.params and setParams are Record<string, number>. min and max are UI hints only (the probe accepted 99999). collectParams (graph.ts:159-176) reuses the ParamDef type for graph-level 'node.param' keys. Scalars that TouchDesigner would set as parameters (width, height, sceneSize) are passed here as 'number' wires from $env. From my own knowledge: TouchDesigner parameters have many types (float, int, toggle, menu, string, XY, RGB) and each can be a constant, an expression, an export or a bind.
kernel/params-model.recommendation: Widen ParamDef to a tagged union with typed values, and plan for a binding value (to env, later to channels) that can replace the scalar $env wires.
kernel/params-model.verifyNote: ParamDef = NumericParamDef | EnumParamDef (types.ts:47-68), with numeric enum values. NodeInstance.params and setParams take Record<string, number>. collectParams reuses ParamDef for 'node.param' keys (graph.ts:159-176). Width and height arrive as 'number' wires from $env. From my own knowledge, TouchDesigner parameters are typed and can be constants, expressions, exports or binds.

kernel/unseeded-noise.title: Noise fields ignore the seed: the fixed permutation table with no seed or offset param
kernel/unseeded-noise.evidence: noise-utils.ts:2-21 hard-codes Ken Perlin's reference permutation. perlin-noise.ts and simplex-noise.ts declare only a noiseScale param (simplex-noise.ts:73-75), and only domain-warp has offsetX/offsetY params. Every patch therefore renders the same noise landscape whatever env.rng's seed. From my own knowledge: hash-seeded generative works like Meridian and Subscapes vary their noise per seed (for example, canvas-sketch-util's random.setSeed reseeds noise2D).
kernel/unseeded-noise.recommendation: Derive a per-seed permutation or coordinate offset from the kernel's per-node RNG. Pass it to the GLSL path as a uniform (field-render compiles fields to GLSL). Pin it with golden values.
kernel/unseeded-noise.verifyNote: noise-utils.ts hard-codes Perlin's reference permutation. perlin-noise.ts:46 and simplex-noise.ts:74 declare only noiseScale. Only domain-warp has offsetX/offsetY (domain-warp.ts:29-30). Nothing reads env.rng in the noise path, so every seed gets the same noise landscape. From my own knowledge, canvas-sketch-util's random.setSeed reseeds its noise functions.

kernel/root-barrel-incoherent.title: The root index.ts mixes kernel API, generic-named field builders, the stdlib registry and one patch
kernel/root-barrel-incoherent.evidence: index.ts:31-43 exports ~30 FieldExpr builders with generic names at the package root (X, Y, c, u, add, sub, mul, div, abs, neg, floor, round, clamp, mix, apply...). index.ts:70-165 imports all 37 operators, defines allOperators and createDefaultRegistry in the root file rather than in operators/, and re-exports exactly one patch (meridianGraph, index.ts:158), while the other 13 patches are reachable only via the ./patches subpath. Importing '@node-td/engine' to get CookEngine therefore loads every operator and render/webgl (pulled in by field-render.ts:4 and grid-sampler.ts:4). package.json declares sideEffects:false, but index.ts's eager imports of allOperators keep everything reachable.
kernel/root-barrel-incoherent.recommendation: Give the kernel its own entry point (exporting the data model, graph utilities, CookEngine, OperatorRegistry, SeededRNG). Export the field algebra as a namespace. Move allOperators and createDefaultRegistry into operators/index.ts. Export patches only from ./patches.
kernel/root-barrel-incoherent.verifyNote: index.ts:31-43 exports X, Y, c, u, add, sub, mul, div, abs, neg, floor, round, clamp, mix, apply, etc. at the package root. index.ts:70-165 imports every operator, defines allOperators and createDefaultRegistry, and re-exports only meridianGraph (14 graphs exist in ./patches). Importing CookEngine therefore pulls in render/webgl through field-render.ts:4 and grid-sampler.ts:4. operators/index.ts also exports the noise primitives pnoise and simplex2 next to the operators.

kernel/graph-snapshot-no-edit-api.title: CookEngine snapshots the topology; any graph edit means a new engine and loss of the whole cache
kernel/graph-snapshot-no-edit-api.evidence: The topology indices are readonly and built once (cook.ts:44-108). Probe: adding node c to the graph object after construction leaves getOutput('c') undefined. frame.tsx (~111) builds a new CookEngine whenever graph identity changes, throwing away every cached output. The node editor in packages/frame/src/editor will make structural edits often.
kernel/graph-snapshot-no-edit-api.recommendation: Either add structural edit methods that patch the indices and dirty affected descendants, or carry cached outputs over into a new engine for unchanged nodes. Treat Graph as immutable (freeze it in dev) so live instance.params reads cannot drift from the snapshot.
kernel/graph-snapshot-no-edit-api.verifyNote: Probe: adding node c after construction leaves getOutput('c') undefined. frame.tsx:111 and editor-preview.tsx:28 rebuild the engine on any change of graph identity. A related inconsistency: the topology is snapshotted, but instance.params is read live at cook time (cook.ts:192, 225-226), so editing graph.nodes[k].params in place takes effect only when something else dirties k.

kernel/dead-kernel-surface.title: Unused kernel surface: Operator.shader, Signal/'signal', the CHOP placeholder, RNG fork, duplicate terminal helpers

SeededRNG.fork (rng.ts:42) has no callers. terminalOutputs and findTerminalOutput in graph.ts:181-217 duplicate CookEngine.findTerminalOutput and are used only by the index.ts re-export. validateGraph is exported but called nowhere.

kernel/kernel-untested.title: No tests pin the cook semantics, which already diverge between Frame and EditorPreview
kernel/kernel-untested.evidence: No test files and no test script exist (package.json scripts: clean, typecheck). The two hosts drive the same engine differently: frame.tsx clears the cache every draw, editor-preview.tsx does not. As a result the determinism bug (rng-shared-stream), the env bypass (implicit-env-reads), setParams aliasing and the composite mutation all appear only in the incremental path that is not exercised in production. Add a property test that a full cook equals an incremental cook under random param edits, golden headless cooks of each patch up to the ROP nodes (later with a stub createCanvas), and a turbo test task.

kernel/seed-owned-by-host.title: A graph cannot declare its seed: Frame uses 42 and EditorPreview uses 149149941, so the same patch renders differently in the gallery and the editor
kernel/seed-owned-by-host.evidence: Graph (graph.ts:18-23) has only id, name, nodes and wires, with no seed. frame.tsx:141 passes `rng: new SeededRNG(42)` and editor-preview.tsx:66 passes `rng: new SeededRNG(149149941)`. Nine of the 14 shipped graphs contain an RNG-consuming node (poisson-disc, circle-pack, dash-stroke, binary-subdivide; probe), so each looks different in the two hosts, apart from EditorPreview's different virtual size. A patch that reverse-engineers a specific seeded output has no place to record that seed.
kernel/seed-owned-by-host.recommendation: Put the seed on the Graph (or as a declared env input with a per-graph default) and have every host pass it through. Combine this with the per-node seeding in rng-shared-stream.

kernel/buffer2d-float32-rgba.title: Buffer2D's only storage is Float32Array, and stroke-renderer reads back every rendered frame into it eagerly, the root of the memory blowup behind clearCache
kernel/buffer2d-float32-rgba.evidence: types.ts:90-97 gives Buffer2D a single `data: Float32Array`, so a rendered RGBA frame costs 16 bytes per pixel. stroke-renderer's canvasBuffer (stroke-renderer.ts:355-370, called at :159, :223, :339) runs getImageData and a per-pixel /255 Float32 conversion on every cook, while also attaching _canvas. Both consumers prefer _canvas: blitBuffer2D (canvas-2d.ts:136-139) and composite's fast path (composite.ts:60). In the common single-layer patches the Float32 copy is therefore computed and cached but never read. point-renderer.ts:89 does the same. The memory comments (frame.tsx:159-161 '~100 MB per panel at 2× DPR', cook.ts:286-289 '600 MB+') follow from this representation, not only from cache retention.
kernel/buffer2d-float32-rgba.recommendation: Let buffer storage be typed per use: Uint8 RGBA, or a canvas/texture-backed handle with lazy readback, for rendered frames, and Float32 for scalar fields and heightmaps. Make readback lazy and owned by the render layer. Do this before designing cache budgets.

kernel/rng-seed-entropy.title: SeededRNG collapses seeds to 32 bits: fractional and ≥2^32 numeric seeds collide, and string hashes go through 32-bit FNV-1a
kernel/rng-seed-entropy.evidence: rng.ts:21 hashes strings with FNV-1a to 32 bits (rng.ts:47-54), and splitmix32 applies `| 0` (rng.ts:59). Probe: new SeededRNG(1), new SeededRNG(1.5) and new SeededRNG(1 + 2**32) all return 0.3312010809313506 as their first draw. A 64-hex-char token hash reduces to one 32-bit value (1886813109 for '0x'+'ab'*32). The header claims the same family as fxhash and Art Blocks. From my own knowledge, those seed sfc32's four state words directly from separate 32-bit slices of the hash, so this seeding cannot reproduce their streams and has birthday collisions around 2^16 tokens.
kernel/rng-seed-entropy.recommendation: Accept a hex hash or a bigint and seed a, b, c and d from four 32-bit slices (the fxhash/Art Blocks convention). Reject non-integer numeric seeds. Pin with golden-value tests.

kernel/needscook-ignores-env.title: needsCook does not reflect env changes, because the env diff happens only inside cook(env)
kernel/needscook-ignores-env.evidence: needsCook (cook.ts:299-301) returns dirty.size > 0, but env-driven dirtying happens only at the start of cook(env) (cook.ts:168-177). A host that writes `if (engine.needsCook) engine.cook(env)`, which is what the getter invites, would never re-cook on resize. No current host uses needsCook (grep), so this is latent.
kernel/needscook-ignores-env.recommendation: Move env diffing into an explicit setEnv(env) step, the counterpart of setParams, so needsCook is accurate, and make cook() take no env or assert that it equals the last setEnv.

kernel/env-magic-string.title: $env is a magic string pseudo-node, special-cased in 17 places across four files, with no declared outputs
kernel/env-magic-string.evidence: `"$env"` appears 17 times in kernel/cook.ts, kernel/graph.ts, editor/types.ts and frame/src/editor/editor-canvas.tsx (grep, excluding patches). Each site re-derives what $env is. editor/types.ts:59-63 inferEnvPortType returns "number" on both branches of its if, so env port types are guessed. Nothing stops a node from being keyed '$env' or a wire from targeting '$env' (topoSort would then report a spurious 'Graph contains a cycle').
kernel/env-magic-string.recommendation: Represent the environment as a declared source: a reserved node with typed outputs defined once in the kernel, or graph-level env inputs. Have cook, validate, topoSort and the editor all read that one declaration.

field/compiler-infinite-loop.title: compileField never terminates for any expression that contains fbm, warp or apply
field/compiler-infinite-loop.evidence: genFunctions iterates `for (const [expr, name] of ctx.functions)` (field-compiler.ts:279). For every function that is not fbm or warp it calls genExprAsBody (318). That function does `ctx.functions.delete(expr)` and then `ctx.functions.set(expr, saved)` (336-339), which appends the entry to the end of the Map currently being iterated, so it is visited again, forever. Map iteration visits entries re-added during iteration; I checked this in bun (a delete-and-reset loop was still iterating after 11 visits on a 2-entry Map). Running compileField in bun: simplex alone compiles; fbmExpr(simplex) and warp-of-fbm were killed by an 8 s alarm (exit 142). Cooking terrainHeightmapGraph in bun with no GL finishes in 29 ms. With a stub `env._gl = {canvas:{...}}` it never returns, because the loop starts before any GL call and throws nothing, so the try/catch at field-render.ts:81-89 cannot rescue it. Frame passes `_gl: getSharedGL()` (frame.tsx:142), so the gallery's Terrain Heightmap panel should freeze the browser main thread. The browser effect is inferred from code plus the bun reproduction.
field/compiler-infinite-loop.recommendation: Make codegen pure. Pass the expression being defined to genExpr as an excluded 'self' instead of deleting and re-inserting it, and iterate over a fixed, post-ordered list (this also fixes glsl-declaration-order). Add a bun test that compileField terminates and returns source for the FieldExpr of every field operator and of every patch's field chain.
field/compiler-infinite-loop.verifyNote: Read field-compiler.ts:276-342. genFunctions iterates ctx.functions (279); for a non-fbm/warp entry genExprAsBody deletes and re-sets the same key (336-340), which appends it to the end of the Map being iterated, so it is visited again forever. Reproduced in bun with a 5 s kill: compileField(simplex) returns; compileField(fbmExpr(simplex,...)) was killed (exit 143). Each pass also pushes lines, so in a browser it is a hang that grows memory until the tab dies. Reachability is real: Frame passes _gl: getSharedGL() (frame.tsx:142), field-render.getGL returns it (field-render.ts:20-28) and calls compileField (84) before any GL call, and the gallery's Terrain Heightmap is simplex→fbm→field-remap→field-render (terrain-heightmap.ts:16-28). The bug dates from the first compiler commit (d73fd8a). The main checkout's uncommitted work does not change field-compiler.ts.

field/glsl-declaration-order.title: GLSL helper functions are emitted before the functions they call (use before declaration)
field/glsl-declaration-order.evidence: registerFn assigns a name before analyzing the children (field-compiler.ts:196-203), and genFunctions emits in Map insertion order, which is pre-order. A caller is therefore emitted before the callees it registers. GLSL requires a function to be declared before it is called. I made a scratch copy in $TMPDIR that iterates a snapshot (`[...ctx.functions]`) to get past the hang. It reported 'curl-of-ridge: field_fn_2 used before defined' for apply(abs(2*fbm(simplex)-1)), which is the curl/gradient-of-ridge chain the subscapes debug patches feed to grid-sampler. It reported 'warp-of-fbm: field_fn_1 used before defined' for warp(fbm(simplex), simplex). Plain fbm was emitted in a valid order.
field/glsl-declaration-order.recommendation: Emit functions in post-order: assign a name only after the children have been analyzed, or topologically sort the function-call graph, or emit prototypes for every field_fn first. Add a structural test that no field_fn_N is referenced before its definition, covering nested fbm/warp/apply.
field/glsl-declaration-order.verifyNote: registerFn names a node before analyzing its children (196-203). I copied the compiler to $TMPDIR, changed only the loop to iterate [...ctx.functions], and checked whether any field_fn_N is used before its definition. fbm(simplex): valid order. warp(fbm(simplex), simplex): field_fn_1 is used before it is defined. apply(abs(2*fbm(simplex)-1), x+1, y): the emitted field_fn_0 body calls field_fn_2, which is defined below it. GLSL ES needs a prototype or definition before a call. Today the hang masks this bug. Once the hang is fixed, the empty catch would turn it into a silent CPU fallback. Note: the apply-based domain rotation that duplicate-closure-fallbacks recommends would hit this bug too.

field/glsl-number-literals.title: glFloat and neg produce invalid GLSL for exponent, non-finite and negative constants
field/glsl-number-literals.evidence: glFloat appends '.0' when n.toString() has no '.' (field-compiler.ts:208-211). Running compileField in bun showed that mul(X, c(1e-7)) produces `(x * 1e-7.0)`. Values such as 1e21, Infinity and NaN would likewise become `1e+21.0`, `Infinity.0` and `NaN.0`. neg emits `(-${...})` (line 253), so neg(c(-5)) produced `float value = (--5.0);`, which is GLSL's decrement operator applied to an rvalue, a compile error. These errors are then swallowed by the catch blocks (see silent-gpu-fallback).
field/glsl-number-literals.recommendation: Format literals with a mantissa that always contains '.' (handle exponent form), throw on non-finite values, and emit unary minus as `(-(e))`. Unit-test the formatter.
field/glsl-number-literals.verifyNote: Reproduced in bun: mul(X, c(1e-7)) gives `(x * 1e-7.0)` and neg(c(-5)) gives `(--5.0)`; both are invalid GLSL. Non-finite values would also fail. However, no operator or patch can produce these today. Operator parameters reach the shader as uniforms (u()), the only c() literals in operators are small positive constants (0.7, 0.3, 1, 2, 0.5, π, 2π), and the only neg() call wraps a parenthesized mul (curl-noise.ts:65). A negative literal after a binary operator, such as `(x + -1.0)`, is valid GLSL. The bug is latent and reachable only through the public builders and compileField that src/index.ts exports.

field/gpu-cpu-coordinate-mismatch.title: GPU path samples fields at buffer-pixel or grid-index coordinates; the CPU path samples logical pixel coordinates
field/gpu-cpu-coordinate-mismatch.evidence: The shader uses x = gl_FragCoord.x, y = uResolution.y - gl_FragCoord.y (field-compiler.ts:391-392) and has no scale or origin uniform. field-render's CPU path samples field(col*invScale, row*invScale) with invScale = 1/(scale*dpr) (field-render.ts:94-97); the GPU path ignores scale and dpr, so at dpr 2 it renders the field at twice the frequency. grid-sampler's CPU path samples field(col*resolution, row*resolution) (grid-sampler.ts:56), but its GPU path renders a cols×rows target, so it samples at grid indices (col+0.5, row+0.5). Commit 4a0bc7c moved only the CPU path to pixel positions; the comment at subscapes-terrain-3d.ts:66-70 tunes flow noiseScale 0.00025 for pixel positions. In the browser, once cols*rows > 500 (for example a 400x400 panel at resolution 18), Simplex Field, Flow Field and Subscapes Terrain 3D take the GPU path. Their expressions compile, because they have no fbm or apply, so the flow field is evaluated at 1/18 to 1/25 of its intended frequency. There is also a half-pixel offset between pixel centres and the CPU's integer samples.
field/gpu-cpu-coordinate-mismatch.recommendation: Define one sampling convention: an origin and a step per axis, at sample corners or at centres. Pass it to the shader as uniforms and to the CPU loop as the same numbers, behind one rasterize(field, grid) used by both field-render and grid-sampler.
field/gpu-cpu-coordinate-mismatch.verifyNote: The shader sets x = gl_FragCoord.x and y = uResolution.y - gl_FragCoord.y (field-compiler.ts:391-392), with no scale or origin uniform. field-render's CPU path samples col/(scale*dpr) (field-render.ts:94-97), so the GPU path ignores both scale and dpr. grid-sampler's GPU path renders a cols×rows target (grid-sampler.ts:34-38), so it samples at (col+0.5, row+0.5), while the CPU samples col*resolution (56). The comment at subscapes-terrain-3d.ts:66-69 assumes pixel positions. Reachability, from the gallery CSS (routes/index.tsx: max-w-7xl, px-6, gap-6, md:2 / lg:3 columns): at lg widths a panel is about 395px, giving 22×22 or 20×20 grids (CPU path). At md widths a panel is about 464-475px, so Flow Field (resolution 20 → 24×24) and Subscapes Terrain 3D (resolution 18 → 26×26) exceed 500 cells and take the GPU path. In a single column above roughly 560px, all three grid-sampler panels do. The output therefore depends on the viewport width. Their expressions have no fbm or apply, so they compile.

field/cpu-gpu-noise-differ.title: CPU and GPU Perlin and simplex are different algorithms, so output depends on which backend ran
field/cpu-gpu-noise-differ.evidence: CPU pnoise is Ken Perlin's improved noise: the permutation table P (noise-utils.ts), 4 diagonal gradients via `hash & 3`, period 256 (perlin-noise.ts:14-37). GPU perlinNoise uses a sin-fract hash that returns continuous random gradients (field-compiler.ts:31-52). Its comment 'Quintic fade (matches CPU)' is the only thing the two share. CPU simplex2 is Gustavson's: P lookups, 8 gradients (GRAD2), scale 70 (simplex-noise.ts:11-65). GPU simplexNoise is the Ashima/McEwan webgl-noise mod289/permute variant with ring-generated gradients and scale 130 (field-compiler.ts:54-83). I identified the GLSL sources from my own knowledge. Which backend runs depends on whether env has a GL context and whether the grid exceeds 500 cells, so the same patch renders differently in bun and in the browser, and at different panel sizes. The sin hash at large arguments is also precision-sensitive across GPUs (my knowledge).
field/cpu-gpu-noise-differ.recommendation: Keep one authoritative noise definition: a 256-entry permutation as a uniform array or an R8 texture with integer indexing in GLSL ES 3.00. Keep the CPU code in one kernel noise module, and add bun conformance tests that compare evalExpr against a JS transliteration of the emitted GLSL at fixed points.
field/cpu-gpu-noise-differ.verifyNote: The CPU pnoise is permutation-table improved Perlin with `hash & 3` gradients (perlin-noise.ts:14-37). The GLSL perlinNoise uses a sin-fract hashGrad with continuous gradients (field-compiler.ts:31-51). The CPU simplex2 uses the P table, GRAD2 % 8 and scale 70 (simplex-noise.ts:11-65). The GLSL version is the mod289/permute variant with scale 130 (54-82). Identifying these as the Gustavson and Ashima/McEwan algorithms is from my own knowledge. The algorithms, and so the outputs and value ranges, differ. Because the backend is chosen by the presence of _gl, the 500-cell threshold and the viewport width (see the coordinate finding), the same patch renders differently by environment and by window size.

field/noise-unseeded.title: Noise has no seed; separate noise nodes are correlated copies of the same lattice
field/noise-unseeded.evidence: P is a fixed constant (noise-utils.ts:2-22). Neither the perlin nor the simplex FieldExpr node has a seed field (field-expr.ts:30-31). The GLSL hash constants are fixed. GraphEnv.rng exists (types.ts:201-205), but no field operator reads it. subscapes-terrain-3d.ts:65 labels the flow field 'INDEPENDENT simplex noise', yet it is simplex2 on the same lattice as the terrain `noise` node; only the scale differs (0.00025 against 0.012). From my own knowledge, not checked here: TouchDesigner's Noise TOP has Seed, Period, Harmonics, Exponent and Offset parameters, and Matt DesLauriers' sketches typically use canvas-sketch-util/random with setSeed and noise2D.
field/noise-unseeded.recommendation: Carry a seed in the noise FieldExpr nodes, as a seed-permuted table or a seed-derived offset, so every backend honours it. Add a seed param to the noise operators.
field/noise-unseeded.verifyNote: P is a fixed constant (noise-utils.ts:2-22). The perlin and simplex nodes have no seed (field-expr.ts:30-31). GraphEnv.rng exists (types.ts:201-205) and is read only by SOPs (poisson-disc, circle-pack, dash-stroke, binary-subdivide), never by a field operator. The 'INDEPENDENT simplex noise' at subscapes-terrain-3d.ts:65,70 is the same simplex2 lattice at a different scale. 'Correlated copies' is somewhat overstated at very different scales, but two noise nodes at the same scale are identical, and every patch shares one lattice. My knowledge of TouchDesigner's Noise TOP Seed parameter and of the canvas-sketch-util random.setSeed habit is not checked here.

field/grid-sampler-context-per-cook.title: grid-sampler creates and leaks a new WebGL2 context on every cook
field/grid-sampler-context-per-cook.evidence: grid-sampler.ts:32-36 calls env.createCanvas(cols, rows) and then createWebGL2 on every evaluate where cols*rows > 500. The context is never released (no WEBGL_lose_context). Because programCache is a WeakMap keyed by the context (webgl.ts:82), every cook also recompiles the shader. Frame re-cooks on every resize (frame.tsx draw()). From my own knowledge: browsers cap live WebGL contexts (about 16 in Chrome) and drop the oldest, which can be the shared `_sharedGL` (frame.tsx:14-22) that field-render depends on, and nothing calls isContextLost. The uncommitted diff in the main checkout replaces this with env._gl, which confirms the problem. The GPU path gives no benefit here: a grid of a few thousand cells is cheap on CPU (a full 30k-pixel fbm terrain cooked in 29 ms in bun).
field/grid-sampler-context-per-cook.recommendation: Delete grid-sampler's GPU path: the grids are at most a few thousand cells and cheap on CPU. Any GPU rasterization should go through one injected rasterizer that owns a single context. Remove the same fallback from field-render.getGL.
field/grid-sampler-context-per-cook.verifyNote: grid-sampler.ts:32-36 calls env.createCanvas(cols, rows) and createWebGL2 on every evaluate where cols*rows > 500, with no release. programCache is a WeakMap keyed by context (webgl.ts:82), so every cook recompiles the shader. Frame calls engine.clearCache() after every draw (frame.tsx, in draw()), so every resize or param change re-cooks grid-sampler and creates another context. It is reached at md and single-column widths (see the coordinate finding). That browsers cap live WebGL contexts and evict the oldest, possibly _sharedGL, is from my knowledge. The main checkout's uncommitted grid-sampler diff switches to env._gl, which confirms the author saw the problem. field-render.ts:31-36 has the same create-per-cook fallback when a host gives createCanvas but no _gl.

field/silent-gpu-fallback.title: GPU failures are swallowed by an empty catch, hiding shader bugs
field/silent-gpu-fallback.evidence: `catch { // GPU failed — fall through to CPU }` at field-render.ts:87-89 and grid-sampler.ts:47-49. compileShader builds a detailed error containing the full shader source (webgl.ts:37-41), and then nothing reads it. The literal and declaration-order bugs would therefore never surface; the patch just silently runs on CPU, with different noise. A hang (compiler-infinite-loop) is not an exception at all.
field/silent-gpu-fallback.recommendation: Record the fallback reason, for example in cook stats or an env logger, tag each buffer with the backend that produced it, and fail loudly on shader compile errors in development.
field/silent-gpu-fallback.verifyNote: field-render.ts:87-89 and grid-sampler.ts:47-49 both use an empty catch. compileShader builds an error message with the info log and the full source (webgl.ts:37-41), and nothing reads it. A declaration-order or literal error would therefore show up only as different output, coming from the CPU path with different noise. A hang is not an exception, so the catch cannot help with it.

field/render-backend-inside-engine.title: WebGL and GLSL code sit inside the engine; operators reach into render/ and an untyped env._gl
field/render-backend-inside-engine.evidence: Both TOP operators import createWebGL2 and renderFieldToBuffer from ../../render/webgl directly (field-render.ts:4, grid-sampler.ts:4). field-render pulls the context through `(env as Record<string, unknown> | undefined)?._gl as WebGL2RenderingContext` (field-render.ts:20), and dpr through another cast (line 74), because GraphEnv is `Record<string, unknown> & {createCanvas?, rng?}` (types.ts:201-205). The GLSL backend (field-compiler.ts) lives in kernel/, and module-level WeakMap caches live in render/webgl.ts:82,158. Context creation and sharing policy lives in the React package (frame.tsx:14-22).
field/render-backend-inside-engine.recommendation: Add a typed capability to GraphEnv (for example `rasterizer?: FieldRasterizer` and a typed `dpr`), with a CPU implementation in the engine. Move only WebGL context, program and FBO management behind it, in render/ or a separate package. Keep compileField in the kernel as a pure, tested emitter.
field/render-backend-inside-engine.verifyNote: The facts hold. Both TOPs import from ../../render/webgl (field-render.ts:4, grid-sampler.ts:4); _gl is reached through casts (field-render.ts:20) and so is dpr (74); GraphEnv is Record<string,unknown> & {createCanvas?, rng?} (types.ts:201-205); context policy lives in frame.tsx:14-22. The finding omits that render/ is already a separate subpath export (package.json exports './render') and that webgl.ts has no top-level DOM access, so the engine imports and cooks fine in plain bun (I cooked terrain-heightmap in bun). The real problem is the untyped _gl/dpr side channel, not where the files sit. Moving field-compiler.ts out would be a mistake: it is pure string codegen and is most useful kept beside FieldExpr, where bun can test it.

field/kernel-operator-import-cycle.title: kernel/field-expr.ts imports noise from operators/top, which import kernel/field-expr (circular; kernel depends on operators)
field/kernel-operator-import-cycle.evidence: field-expr.ts:1-2 imports pnoise and simplex2 from ../operators/top/*. perlin-noise.ts:3 and simplex-noise.ts:3 import createField, X, Y, c, u and the other builders from ../../kernel/field-expr. noise-utils.ts, which holds only P, sits loose at src/ root. The cycle works only because every cross-use happens at call time. The uncommitted field-jit.ts adds another kernel-to-operators import of the same two functions.
field/kernel-operator-import-cycle.recommendation: Move P, pnoise and simplex2 into a kernel noise module, for example src/kernel/noise/. The interpreters, the JIT and the noise operators import from there, and operators keep only the Operator definitions.
field/kernel-operator-import-cycle.verifyNote: field-expr.ts:1-2 imports pnoise and simplex2 from ../operators/top/*. perlin-noise.ts:3 and simplex-noise.ts:3 import builders from ../../kernel/field-expr. It works only because no module uses the other's exports at top level. noise-utils.ts sits at the src root. The main checkout's uncommitted kernel/field-jit.ts:4-5 adds the same kernel-to-operators imports.

field/duplicate-closure-fallbacks.title: Every field operator implements its semantics twice (FieldExpr and closure); the only in-engine opaque producer is avoidable
field/duplicate-closure-fallbacks.evidence: Each operator has a FieldExpr branch and a hand-written closure fallback: fbm.ts:57-75, domain-warp.ts:50-54, field-math.ts:61-72, field-remap.ts:94-114 (with its own smoothstep copy at 21-24), field-gradient.ts:64-65, curl-noise.ts:71-84. The fallbacks only run when an input is opaque. Inside the engine, the only opaque producer is fbm with domainRotation != 0 (fbm.ts:40, 'domain rotation not yet supported in GLSL'), and Meridian uses it (meridian.ts:45, 0.646). Rotation is expressible today: apply(fbmExpr(src,...), X*cos - Y*sin, X*sin + Y*cos) samples source(rx*freq, ry*freq), exactly like the closure. Nothing tests that the two branches of an operator agree.
field/duplicate-closure-fallbacks.recommendation: After fixing the compiler, express domain rotation as apply(fbm, rotated X, rotated Y). Add an explicit opaque leaf ({tag:'extern', fn}) that CPU backends evaluate and the GPU backend rejects with a reported reason. Then delete the per-operator closure branches.
field/duplicate-closure-fallbacks.verifyNote: The duplication is real: every field operator has an expression branch and a closure branch (fbm.ts:57-75, domain-warp.ts:50-54, field-math.ts:61-72, field-remap.ts:94-114 with its own smoothstep at 21-24, field-gradient.ts:64-65, curl-noise.ts:71-84), and no test compares the two. It is not dead code, though: Meridian uses fbm domainRotation 0.646 (meridian.ts:45), so the fbm and field-remap closures run on every Meridian cook. The apply-based rotation is mathematically equivalent to the closure (I checked rx/ry against fbm.ts:59-68). In GLSL, however, it would register the fbm before its source, and with the current compiler it would hit both the hang and the declaration-order bug. It depends on those fixes landing first.

field/cpu-interpreter-perf.title: CPU tree-walk re-evaluates constant parameters per sample; full-resolution field-render takes about 3 s
field/cpu-interpreter-perf.evidence: evalExpr recurses for every node at every sample and re-evaluates the fbm parameters (octaves, lacunarity, gain, amplitude) on each call (field-expr.ts:151-154). There is no constant folding or common-subexpression elimination. In bun 1.3.9, cooking terrain-heightmap at width 1200, height 800, dpr 2 (a 2400x1600 buffer through the CPU fallback) took 2897 ms. Eight SOPs also sample fields on CPU, so this cost applies outside field-render too. The uncommitted field-jit.ts adds a `new Function` JIT as a third interpreter.
field/cpu-interpreter-perf.recommendation: Add one lowering pass (constant folding, hoisting sample-invariant params, sharing common subexpressions) that both a JS closure or JIT backend and the GLSL emitter consume. Keep evalExpr as the reference, with conformance and benchmark tests in bun.
field/cpu-interpreter-perf.verifyNote: Reproduced: cooking terrainHeightmapGraph at 1200×800, dpr 2, in bun took 2895 ms for a 2400×1600 buffer. A hand-written loop doing the same simplex2 fbm and ridge took 866 ms, so tree-walk overhead is about 3.3×. Re-evaluating the fbm params per sample (field-expr.ts:151-154) is a small part of that; most of it is per-node dispatch and recursion. Eight SOP files take Field2D inputs, so the cost is not limited to field-render.

field/gpu-readback-roundtrip.title: GPU field result is read back as RGBA32F and blitted again, with oversized allocations per cook
field/gpu-readback-roundtrip.evidence: renderFieldToBufferHQ allocates `new Float32Array(width*height*4)` and reads all four channels although only R is used (webgl.ts:302-314). For 2400x1600 that is about 61 MB, plus a 15 MB output, per cook, with a synchronous GPU stall. Frame then converts it back to Uint8 and calls putImageData (canvas-2d.ts:142-170): GPU to CPU to GPU. field-render resizes the shared context's default canvas to the full buffer size (field-render.ts:23-27) although the HQ path renders into an FBO, so a full-size drawing buffer is allocated and never used. preserveDrawingBuffer:true (webgl.ts:206) is not needed for an immediate readPixels. The main checkout's uncommitted renderFieldToTexture works on this.
field/gpu-readback-roundtrip.recommendation: Keep GPU results as textures behind a buffer handle and read back lazily when a CPU consumer needs data. Use R32F where it can be rendered to, and query IMPLEMENTATION_COLOR_READ_FORMAT before reading. Resize the default canvas only on the fallback path.
field/gpu-readback-roundtrip.verifyNote: The cost is real. The RGBA32F readback allocates Float32Array(w*h*4) and uses only R (webgl.ts:302-314): about 61 MB at 2400×1600, plus a 15 MB output, then a CPU conversion and putImageData (canvas-2d.ts:142-170). Two parts are overstated. Resizing the default canvas (field-render.ts:23-27) is used whenever the EXT_color_buffer_float fallback renders into the default framebuffer (webgl.ts:275-278), so it is not always unused. From my knowledge, a WebGL2 readPixels from an R32F target is only guaranteed for RGBA/FLOAT unless IMPLEMENTATION_COLOR_READ_FORMAT allows RED, so an R32F target alone does not shrink the readback. Today this path is unreachable in the gallery, because the only field-render patch hangs in compileField first.

field/gl-resource-lifecycle.title: Programs, VAOs and VBOs are never freed, and context loss is not handled
field/gl-resource-lifecycle.evidence: Every new fragment source creates a program plus its own VAO and VBO holding the identical quad (webgl.ts:107-116). The VBO is never deleted, and the per-context program Map never evicts. Structural param changes (field-remap mode, field-math mode) each add a program. frame.tsx caches `_sharedGL` forever, and there is no webglcontextlost listener and no isContextLost check, so after a loss every cook falls back to CPU silently.
field/gl-resource-lifecycle.recommendation: Share one quad VBO per context, bound the program cache (LRU with deleteProgram), handle context loss and restore, and own all of this in the render layer.
field/gl-resource-lifecycle.verifyNote: Each new fragment source creates its own VAO and VBO for an identical quad (webgl.ts:107-116). The VBO handle is dropped and never deleted, and the per-context program Map never evicts. frame.tsx:14-22 caches _sharedGL forever, and nothing listens for webglcontextlost or checks isContextLost. EditorPreview also creates one context per mounted preview (editor-preview.tsx:8-11,24) and never releases it.

field/eight-bit-and-range.title: The 8-bit readback path clamps and quantizes, so the GPU range differs from the CPU
field/eight-bit-and-range.evidence: renderFieldToBuffer reads UNSIGNED_BYTE and divides by 255 (webgl.ts:243-255), which clamps to [0,1] and quantizes. grid-sampler's GPU path uses it and then multiplies by 2π (grid-sampler.ts:38-43), giving 256 angle levels of about 1.4°. Signed fields such as field-gradient dx and dy, raw simplex, or fbm with amplitude > 1 are clamped on GPU but not on CPU. renderFieldToBufferHQ silently drops to the 8-bit path when EXT_color_buffer_float is missing (webgl.ts:275-278).
field/eight-bit-and-range.recommendation: Give buffers an explicit pixel format, use a float target for fields, and report rather than silently degrade when float targets are unsupported. Most of this disappears if grid-sampler's GPU path is deleted.
field/eight-bit-and-range.verifyNote: renderFieldToBuffer reads UNSIGNED_BYTE and divides by 255 (webgl.ts:243-255), which clamps to [0,1] and quantizes. grid-sampler's GPU path uses it and multiplies by 2π (grid-sampler.ts:38-43), so angles come in 256 steps. renderFieldToBufferHQ silently drops to that path when EXT_color_buffer_float is missing (275-278). The current grid-sampler inputs are already mapped to 0..1, so the clamp matters mostly for signed fields; the quantization applies always.

field/semantic-edge-mismatch.title: CPU and GLSL semantics differ at edge cases; GLSL codegen duplicates subtrees
field/semantic-edge-mismatch.evidence: fbm octaves: Math.round on CPU (field-expr.ts:151) against an int() truncation in the GLSL loop (field-compiler.ts:293). smoothstep with edge0 >= edge1 and clamp with lo > hi are defined on CPU (field-expr.ts:131-137) but undefined in GLSL. atan(0,0) is undefined in GLSL, which affects curl angles on flat ridge regions; CPU Math.atan2 returns 0. div emits the denominator string twice (field-compiler.ts:239-241), warp emits the amount expression twice (311-312), and analyze/genExpr have no memoization for shared, non-function subtrees.
field/semantic-edge-mismatch.recommendation: Specify edge semantics once (guarded smoothstep and clamp, atan2 at zero) and emit the same guards in every backend. Bind repeated subexpressions to temporaries in the GLSL emitter.
field/semantic-edge-mismatch.verifyNote: div repeats the denominator (field-compiler.ts:239-241) and warp repeats amtExpr (311-312); there is no memoization of shared subtrees. GLSL clamp and smoothstep are undefined for lo>hi and edge0>=edge1, and atan(0,0) is undefined. That much is real. Two points are overstated. The octaves round-versus-int() mismatch cannot be reached through the fbm operator, which rounds before u() (fbm.ts:32,43). The CPU smoothstep is not fully defined either: with lo == hi and v == lo it returns NaN (0/0 → Math.min(1,NaN) → NaN). field-remap's lo/hi sliders (0..1) can produce equal or reversed edges, so the mismatch can be reached from the UI.

field/top-family-misfit.title: Most of top/ are resolution-free field functions rather than TOPs; curl-noise and grid-sampler bake a private angle encoding
field/top-family-misfit.evidence: Eight of the ten operators in top/ (perlin-noise, simplex-noise, fbm, domain-warp, field-math, field-remap, field-gradient, curl-noise) output `type: 'field'`, a lazy (x,y) function, not an image. Only field-render outputs a Buffer2D image; grid-sampler outputs a coarse angle grid. From my own knowledge: a TouchDesigner TOP is a GPU texture with a fixed resolution and pixel format, so these field operators behave like a shader graph or expression network. curl-noise generates no noise: it returns (atan2(-dfdx, dfdy) + π) / 2π of its input (curl-noise.ts:64-66). grid-sampler multiplies by 2π (grid-sampler.ts:42,56) purely to suit flow-tracer, so the two operators are coupled through an undocumented 0..1 ↔ 0..2π convention.
field/top-family-misfit.recommendation: Make Field its own family or port category and keep TOP for Buffer2D or texture producers. Rename curl-noise to curl-angle or have it output a direction. Make the 0..1 to angle mapping an explicit parameter or operator instead of a convention hidden in grid-sampler.
field/top-family-misfit.verifyNote: 8 of the 10 operators in top/ output type 'field' (perlin, simplex, fbm, domain-warp, field-math, field-remap, field-gradient, curl-noise). curl-noise returns (atan2(-dfdx, dfdy)+π)/2π of its input (curl-noise.ts:64-66) and generates no noise. grid-sampler multiplies by 2π (42, 56) to suit flow-tracer. The types.ts comment shows the author meant TOP to cover 'Buffer2D, Field2D'. That TouchDesigner TOPs are fixed-resolution GPU textures with a pixel format is from my knowledge.

field/dead-barrels-and-leftovers.title: Unused barrels, an unused shader helper, a redundant uniform and an unused param

field/naming-leftovers.title: Legacy 'generative' symbol namespace, terse single-letter public exports, a misleading label, and a renderer that mutates cooked data
field/naming-leftovers.evidence: FIELD_EXPR = Symbol.for('generative.field-expr') (field-expr.ts:80) is a leftover from the lightfast app. The engine root exports X, Y, c and u plus abs, floor, round, mix and clamp (src/index.ts:30-43), which collide with common names; fmin, fmax, fpow and fatan2 use a different prefix convention. The field-render label is 'Field Render (GPU)' (field-render.ts:61) although it has a CPU path. blitBuffer2D sets `buffer._canvas = undefined` on its input (canvas-2d.ts:138), so a renderer mutates a cooked, cacheable output.
field/naming-leftovers.recommendation: Rename the symbol and the label, and export the builders under a namespace. Move the mutation to a separate code finding: renderers and composite must not mutate cooked outputs, and canvas release belongs to the cook engine's cache policy.
field/naming-leftovers.verifyNote: Symbol.for('generative.field-expr') is at field-expr.ts:80. The root exports X, Y, c, u, abs, floor, round, mix, clamp next to fmin, fmax, fpow, fatan2 (src/index.ts:30-43). The label 'Field Render (GPU)' is at field-render.ts:61. All confirmed and cosmetic. The blitBuffer2D mutation (`buffer._canvas = undefined`, canvas-2d.ts:138) is not a naming issue: it is a cache-correctness issue, and composite.ts:66,73 does the same to its cached input layers. A re-blit or re-composite of a cached buffer silently takes the slower data path.

field/field-render-scale-param-broken.title: field-render's 'Resolution Scale' parameter produces an image that does not fill the canvas
field/field-render-scale-param-broken.evidence: field-render sizes its output as round(width*scale*dpr) × round(height*scale*dpr) (field-render.ts:75-76). Frame sets the canvas to w*dpr × h*dpr and calls blitBuffer2D, which does putImageData at (0,0) with no scaling (canvas-2d.ts:169-170). EditorPreview likewise drawImages the temp canvas at (0,0) (editor-preview.tsx:75-80). At scale 0.5 the image covers the top-left quarter; at scale 2 it is cropped. The GPU path ignores scale entirely as well (shader samples at gl_FragCoord), so the sampling frequency also changes with scale. The param is exposed in the editor (field-render.ts:69).
field/field-render-scale-param-broken.recommendation: Either remove the scale param, or have the output carry its logical size and have the blit and composite stages scale it to the target (drawImage with a destination size), so scale changes resolution and not framing.

field/field-render-env-outside-dirty-tra.title: field-render reads env.dpr and env._gl outside $env wires, so the incremental cook does not re-cook it when they change
field/field-render-env-outside-dirty-tra.evidence: CookEngine.cook dirties nodes only for keys reached by $env wires (cook.ts, the envDependents loop at the top of cook()). terrain-heightmap wires only width and height into render (terrain-heightmap.ts:26-28). field-render reads env.dpr (field-render.ts:74) and env._gl (20) directly. A DPR change alone, for example moving the window to another monitor without a size change, leaves the cached buffer at the old DPR. This is masked today only because Frame calls engine.clearCache() after every draw; EditorPreview fixes dpr at 1.
field/field-render-env-outside-dirty-tra.recommendation: Make dpr an $env wire, or have the cook engine track which env keys an operator reads, so that dropping clearCache-every-draw (which the incremental cook was built to avoid) does not produce stale output.

field/field-render-context-fallback-per-.title: field-render's own fallback creates a new WebGL2 context on every cook
field/field-render-context-fallback-per-.evidence: When env has no _gl but does have createCanvas, getGL does createCanvas(w, h) then createWebGL2(canvas) on every evaluate (field-render.ts:31-36), with no release. The programCache and FBO cache are keyed by context, so each cook also recompiles and reallocates. Frame and EditorPreview inject _gl, so the gallery avoids this, but any other host (a headless runner, or a future worker) that supplies only createCanvas hits the same leak as grid-sampler.
field/field-render-context-fallback-per-.recommendation: Remove the per-cook context creation. Require an injected rasterizer or context, and fall back to CPU when none is given.

field/editor-preview-context-per-graph.title: EditorPreview creates a WebGL2 context per mounted preview and never releases it
field/editor-preview-context-per-graph.evidence: makeGL() creates an OffscreenCanvas(1,1) WebGL2 context (editor-preview.tsx:8-11) on first render of each component (24). frame-editor.tsx:66 keys EditorPreview by graph.id, so every graph switch mounts a new component and a new context. There is no cleanup or WEBGL_lose_context on unmount, and it does not reuse Frame's _sharedGL. These contexts count toward the browser's live-context limit (the limit is from my knowledge).
field/editor-preview-context-per-graph.recommendation: Use the single shared context, or the injected rasterizer, for previews too, and release contexts on unmount.

sop/geometric-normal-sign.title: geometric-normal gives mirrored or downward normals: its one-sided tangent has the wrong sign
sop/geometric-normal-sign.recommendation: Compute the heightfield normal as normalize(-∂h/∂x, 1, -∂h/∂z) with central differences (or one consistent orientation). Put it in a single shared helper that surface-raymarch also uses. Share the centre sample with surface-lift, or fuse lift and normal, to keep the cost down. Add a bun test with analytic planes. Then fix diffuse-shade's light-direction convention and re-tune the Subscapes light.
sop/geometric-normal-sign.verifyNote: Read geometric-normal.ts:56-89. The backward branches set ty = hCenter-hBack (line 63) and uy = hCenter-hBack (line 77), but P(u-eps)-P(u) has y = hBack-hCenter. Mixing forward and backward branches also flips the orientation of the cross product. I reran it in bun ($TMPDIR scratch) on h=0.5x for eps 1 and 1e-5 and got exactly the reported vectors. Interior (10,10) gives (0.447,0.894,0). x=0 gives (0.447,-0.894,0). z=0 gives (-0.447,-0.894,0). The (0,0) corner, all-forward, is the only correct one. Algebraically, every interior vertex gets n ∝ (∂h/∂x, 1, ∂h/∂z), so normals are mirrored in both X and Z, not only X. diffuse-shade.ts:57-70 consumes them through the cull→shade wire (subscapes-terrain-3d.ts:267). The reader's patch line numbers are about 12-16 lines off: the light is at lines 131-133 and normals at 96-99. Two more things the fix must cover. (1) diffuse-shade computes max(0, N·L) with a default L.y of -0.707, so upward normals get no diffuse at all. Once the normals are fixed, the light convention (N·-L) or the patch light must change too. (2) normals is the most expensive node in Subscapes: 164 ms of a 473 ms SOP cook at 400 px, measured. It evaluates the field again at the same point surface-lift has already sampled.

sop/raymarch-penetration-ao.title: surface-raymarch accepts hits deep under the surface, and its AO measures that error rather than occlusion
sop/raymarch-penetration-ao.recommendation: After a sign change, bisect or secant-refine the hit. Use a Lipschitz-bounded step (dist·k, with k < 1 derived from the maximum slope) or a relaxation parameter. Compute AO along the normal or at horizontal offsets. Make the minimum step a scene-relative parameter.
sop/raymarch-penetration-ao.verifyNote: surface-raymarch.ts:114 accepts any dist < epsilon, including large negatives. Line 120 steps t += max(dist, 0.5) using vertical distance, and there is no refinement. The AO loop (lines 73-82) samples height(wx,wz) at the hit's own column, so an exact hit gives sh = -step < 0 and ao = 1. I cooked the real Meridian graph in bun with SeededRNG(42) at 600 px: 86 hits, 83 penetrating by more than epsilon, worst -34.65. All 63 hits with ao < 1 were penetrating; the reader said 61, which is negligible. At 256 px it was 100 of 113 penetrating, and all 77 ao < 1 hits penetrating. So the AO attribute measures overshoot error, and point-orient uses it to set stroke length. The 45° threshold is loose: the safe slope depends on ray pitch (about 42° for this camera). The conclusion stands.

sop/raymarch-absolute-units.title: Meridian raymarch params are in absolute world units while the camera scales with canvas size, so larger canvases get no hits

maxDist 700, amplitude 80, epsilon 0.3 and min step 0.5 are absolute numbers (surface-raymarch.ts:39-45, 120; meridian.ts:65-73). camera-3d positions the eye relative to sceneSize, which is $env height (meridian.ts:96-98; camera-3d.ts:244-248). Measured raymarch hits per canvas size:
- 300px: 143 hits out of 152 seeds
- 400px: 142 of 265
- 600px: 86 of 582 (496 misses, all from t ≥ maxDist)
- 800px: 0 hits, so the patch renders nothing.
The patch comment (meridian.ts:52-53) shows it was calibrated for sceneSize ≈ 256.

Normalise depth by that range, not by maxDist. Add a test that hit rate and the depth distribution are stable across 256-1600 px.

These match the report exactly. camera-3d.ts:245-249 scales the eye by ss. The ray origin is on the near plane, about 1.76·ss from the target, and maxDist is a fixed 700 (meridian.ts:66-74). The meridian.ts:52-54 comment works out to ss ≈ 256. This is worse than reported: editor-preview.tsx:52-54 cooks at 4× the wrapper size, so the Meridian preview in the editor is blank for any wrapper wider than about 200 px. depth = t/maxDist (line 134) is also size-dependent.

sop/shared-rng-nondeterminism.title: Random SOPs share one RNG stream, so output depends on cook order and which nodes re-cook
sop/shared-rng-nondeterminism.evidence: All four SOPs draw from env.rng (poisson-disc.ts:114, binary-subdivide.ts:54, dash-stroke.ts:16, circle-pack.ts:50). editor-preview.tsx:66 creates a new SeededRNG(149149941) for each cook. cook.ts:168-177 diffs only $env-wired keys, so a param tweak re-cooks just the dirty node, which then reads from the start of the stream instead of where a full cook would be. In subscapes, binary-subdivide cooks before poisson-disc and both draw from the stream, so tweaking poisson-disc alone yields different seeds from a full cook. SeededRNG.fork(tag) (rng.ts:42) exists but nothing uses it. From my knowledge of TouchDesigner, SOPs with randomness (Noise SOP, Sprinkle SOP) each have their own Seed parameter.
sop/shared-rng-nondeterminism.recommendation: Have the kernel inject a per-node RNG built from a hash of (root seed, node key, the node's own seed param), never from the shared stream. Make fork depend only on the original seed, or remove it. Drop the Math.random fallback. Use one root seed in Frame and in EditorPreview.

All four SOPs call env.rng.random() (circle-pack:50, poisson-disc:114, binary-subdivide:54, dash-stroke:16). editor-preview.tsx:66 creates a new SeededRNG for each draw, and setParams and cook re-cook only dirty nodes (cook.ts:134-150). So a poisson-disc tweak re-runs seeds from stream position 0, without binary-subdivide's draws first. The gallery Frame is not affected, because frame.tsx:163 calls clearCache() after every draw, forcing a full cook. The editor (seed 149149941) and the gallery (seed 42) also use different seeds, so the same patch looks different in each. The proposed fix as written does not work. SeededRNG.fork (rng.ts:42-43) mixes in this.d, a counter that random() increments, so fork(tag) on a consumed stream depends on stream position. I confirmed in bun that fork('a') before and after one random() differ. GraphEnv.rng is also typed as { random() } only (types.ts:204), so operators cannot call fork without casting. The TD claim that Noise and Sprinkle have their own Seed parameter matches my own knowledge.

sop/geometry-dim-untyped-strides.title: 2D and 3D geometry share one port type and operators hard-code strides: wrong-dim wiring yields silent garbage
sop/geometry-dim-untyped-strides.evidence:
PortType has a single 'geometry' (types.ts:28), and graph.ts:85 compares only port types. Most operators assume a stride instead of reading geo.dim:
- stride 2: surface-lift (lines 45-46), surface-raymarch (lines 97-98), point-orient fallback (lines 58-59);
- stride 3: project-3d (lines 37-39), geometric-normal (lines 42-44), visibility-cull (lines 68-74, 114-115, 328-330).
Only flow-tracer (lines 46-47) and transform-2d honour dim. transform-2d writes only x and y into a fresh array (lines 34-46): bun shows a 3D input [1,2,3,4,5,6] coming out as [1,2,0,4,5,0], so z is zeroed. merge copies g.vertexCount×dim floats using the first input's dim (lines 39, 66-69), so mixed-dim inputs scramble.
