Either way, validate at wire time. Add an assertDim guard in each SOP. Replace transform-2d with a dim-generic Transform that preserves z and transforms normals.
sop/geometry-dim-untyped-strides.verifyNote: PortType has a single 'geometry' (types.ts:28), and validateGraph compares only port types (graph.ts:85). The stride hard-coding matches every cited line. In bun, transform-2d maps [1,2,3,4,5,6] (dim 3) to [1,2,0,4,5,0]. merge copies vertexCount×dim floats using geos[0].dim (lines 39, 66-69).

sop/geometry-model-gaps.title: Geometry has scalar-only per-vertex attributes, normals stored two ways, no closed flag, and a strip encoding without a terminator
sop/geometry-model-gaps.evidence:
- attributes are one float per vertex (types.ts:123-129), so vectors are split into worldX/Y/Z and normalX/Y/Z channels (surface-raymarch.ts:162-171), while geometric-normal writes geometry.normals as vec3 (geometric-normal.ts:118). Consumers must handle both.
- There are no per-strip (primitive) attributes; diffuse-shade instead fakes per-vertex colour via palette.count === vertexCount (stroke-renderer.ts:245).
- There is no closed flag: base-outline's 'closed loop' (base-outline.ts:16-23) is an open line-strip that only fill-mode closePath closes.
- Each geometry has one topology, so points cannot be merged with lines.
- stripOffsets has no end sentinel, and a missing stripOffsets means one implicit strip (types.ts:113-118, 298-304). In merge, bun shows that inputs [strip without offsets, strip with offsets] give stripOffsets [2], so the first strip disappears.
From my knowledge of TouchDesigner, its SOP geometry has points, primitives (open or closed polygons, meshes) and typed attributes of any size (P, N, Cd, uv) at point, vertex or primitive level.
sop/geometry-model-gaps.recommendation: Use sized attribute classes for point and primitive data. Make N a single canonical attribute. Add a per-primitive closed flag. Make stripOffsets CSR (length strips+1) and always present for line-strip. Carry colour as an attribute (Cd), not through the palette.count heuristic.
sop/geometry-model-gaps.verifyNote: Each claim checks out. Attributes are scalar-only (types.ts:123-129). Normals exist both as a vec3 `normals` (geometric-normal.ts:118) and as normalX/Y/Z attributes (surface-raymarch.ts:168-170). There is no closed flag: base-outline emits stripOffsets [0] (line 96), and the polygon is closed only by closePath in the stroke-renderer fill mode. Each geometry has a single topology. In bun, merge of [implicit strip, explicit strip] gives stripOffsets [2], losing the first strip. stroke-renderer.ts:176 and :245 switch to per-vertex colour whenever palette.count === vertexCount, which is a coincidence-based contract. The TD attribute model matches my own knowledge.

sop/attribute-propagation.title: Attributes, normals and depth are dropped inconsistently as geometry passes through SOPs
sop/attribute-propagation.recommendation: Add kernel helpers withPositions and filterVertices that carry every attribute through, and use them in all modifiers. Have project-3d write a depth attribute.
sop/attribute-propagation.verifyNote: Checked each file. surface-lift.ts:58-66, project-3d.ts:46-55 (which discards the third value of project() at line 41), geometric-normal.ts:110-119, visibility-cull.ts:385-393 and merge.ts:101-110 all rebuild the geometry without attributes. flow-tracer and dash-stroke go through pathsGeometry, so poisson-disc's cellId is lost. transform-2d and point-orient spread ...geometry and keep everything.

sop/visibility-cull-camera-mesh-coupling.title: visibility-cull guesses the camera direction from 4 diagonals and infers grid layout and winding from parametric-surface's index pattern
sop/visibility-cull-camera-mesh-coupling.evidence:
- Eye direction is chosen from candidates [±1,1,±1] by probing project() depth (lines 258-277), and is constant across the scene, so any non-diagonal or perspective camera gets wrong back-face and occlusion tests. Camera3D (types.ts:179-192) exposes no eye or forward vector.
- Grid size is inferred as uSeg = meshIdx[2]−1 (line 128), assuming quads are row-major with 2 triangles each (lines 138-142). Any other triangle mesh silently maps points to the wrong triangles.
- Winding is compensated with a swapped cross product (lines 78-86) and a one-sided det test (lines 228-233), both tied to parametric-surface's TL,TR,BL order (parametric-surface.ts:56-61).
- The docstring says it is 'General-purpose' (lines 25-26).

Either test occlusion by marching the height field toward the eye, or build a real spatial index instead of inferring the grid from the index order. Correct the 'general-purpose' docstring until then.

sop/visibility-cull-quadratic.title: visibility-cull occlusion is O(triangles²)
sop/visibility-cull-quadratic.evidence: isTriangleVisible casts one ray per triangle against every other triangle (lines 296-307); results are cached per triangle, but the first test is a full scan. It also allocates three Float64Arrays per triangle (lines 76, 89, 94-98) and two-element arrays on every lookup (lines 144, 180). Measured in bun with strokes covering every quad: 42×42 (3528 tris) took 57ms, 60×60 took 223ms, 100×100 took 1583ms; 5.7× the triangles cost 28× the time.

sop/visibility-cull-quadratic.verifyNote: isTriangleVisible scans every triangle (lines 296-307). sop/heightfield-param-sprawl.title: Five SOPs each carry their own amplitude (and baseY) for one height field, kept in sync by hand, with defaults that disagree
sop/heightfield-param-sprawl.evidence:
- Defaults disagree: amplitude 120 in surface-lift (line 33) and geometric-normal (line 33); 80 in base-outline (line 38), contour-ring (line 33) and surface-raymarch (line 39).
- subscapes-terrain-3d repeats amplitude:120 and baseY:6 across lift, normals, liftmesh, base and contour (lines 111, 114, 121, 168, 188). The debug patches repeat 80 and 0.
- geometric-normal ignores baseY entirely.
- The field algebra has no unary scale or offset: field-math needs two field inputs (field-math.ts:27-41). That is why every SOP re-scales the field itself.
sop/heightfield-param-sprawl.recommendation: Add a heightfield value (field, amplitude, base, domain), or a unary scale and offset TOP, so the SOPs stop carrying amplitude and baseY. Pick one clamping rule. Until then, align the defaults.
sop/heightfield-param-sprawl.verifyNote: The default disagreement is real: 120 in surface-lift:33 and geometric-normal:33, and 80 in base-outline:38, contour-ring:33 and surface-raymarch:39. The Subscapes patch repeats 120 at lines 95, 98, 104, 142 and 163. Two claims are overstated. 'geometric-normal ignores baseY' is correct behaviour, because a constant offset does not change the gradient. And the field algebra does have a scale, fbm amplitude, though it is capped at 5 and has no offset. There is also an inconsistency the reader missed: surface-lift does not clamp (line 54), while base-outline:55 and contour-ring:52 clamp max(0, field·amp). With a signed field, strokes would dip below the base polygon.

sop/tile-skirt-hardcoded-edges.title: base-outline and contour-ring hard-code which tile edges are visible and duplicate the edge sampling
sop/tile-skirt-hardcoded-edges.evidence: Both always sample the back edge z=h and the right edge x=w with identical loops (base-outline.ts:48-66; contour-ring.ts:44-61). That matches only the Subscapes eye (1,1,1) (subscapes-terrain-3d.ts:122-131). camera-3d's default eye is (0.75, 1.0, −0.75) (camera-3d.ts:216-218). By geometric reasoning, the visible side faces for that eye are x=w and z=0, so these SOPs would draw a hidden edge and omit the visible one. The 4-power easing is hard-coded (contour-ring.ts:70).
sop/tile-skirt-hardcoded-edges.recommendation: Use one tile-boundary sampler that takes the camera or an edge selection, as a Subscapes component. Expose the easing exponent.
sop/tile-skirt-hardcoded-edges.verifyNote: base-outline.ts:48-66 and contour-ring.ts:44-61 both sample z=h and x=w with identical loops. The easing is hard-coded at contour-ring.ts:70. The default camera-3d eye is (0.75, 1, -0.75) (camera-3d.ts:216-218), which by geometry makes x=w and z=0 the visible sides. Every patch currently uses eye (1,1,1), so the bug is latent. The patch line numbers are about 12 lines off.

sop/sop-family-structure.title: The sop/ folder mixes generic SOPs, Subscapes terrain pieces and camera-dependent passes, with no layering
sop/sop-family-structure.evidence:
- project-3d, visibility-cull and surface-raymarch all take a camera3d input and produce screen-space results. surface-raymarch outputs screen positions with world-space attributes (lines 133-138), so one geometry holds two coordinate spaces.
- surface-lift, geometric-normal, base-outline and contour-ring all assume the same X/Z ground plane, Y-up height-field convention.
- base-outline and contour-ring are Subscapes-only; point-orient depends on surface-raymarch's attribute names (point-orient.ts:47-51).
- From my knowledge of TouchDesigner: projection to screen and hidden-surface removal belong to the Render TOP with a Camera COMP, not to SOPs. Reusable sub-networks are Components (COMPs).
- index.ts files group these as 'transforms & 3D pipeline' and 'implicit surface / raymarching' (operators/index.ts:30-42), with no folder structure.
sop/sop-family-structure.recommendation: Use sop/ for generic ops and sop/heightfield/ for lift, normal and raymarch on one heightfield abstraction. Make camera-space passes (project, cull) a separate stage. Move the Subscapes-only skirt and contour ops, and the Meridian length heuristics, into patch-level components.

sop/poisson-partition-density-noop.title: poisson-disc's partition-aware density does nothing in its one patch, and seeds in the margin are never filtered
sop/poisson-partition-density-noop.evidence: Seeds are kept with probability (1−depth)/densityScale + depth (poisson-disc.ts:152), and depth is leafDepth/maxDepth (binary-subdivide.ts:128). With Subscapes params (maxDepth 5, minSize 20, 400px), bun shows all 32 leaves at depth 1.0, so keepProb = 1 everywhere: density was 25.18 per 1000px² inside the partitions and 25.46 in the margin. Seeds outside the partitions (the 100px default margin; partitions cover only [0, h]²) are always kept with cellId −1 (lines 139-143). Random rejection can only thin a blue-noise set, which creates gaps; it cannot add density. Separately, poisson-disc.ts:96 claims 'deeper cells get tighter spacing'.
sop/poisson-partition-density-noop.recommendation: Use a variable-radius Bridson, or run Bridson per cell with r scaled by depth. Make binary-subdivide produce varied depths. Clip or skip seeds outside the partition domain.
sop/poisson-partition-density-noop.verifyNote: I ran binary-subdivide in bun with Subscapes params (5 / 20 / 0.15) at 400 px. It produced 32 leaves, all at normalised depth 1, so keepProb = 1 everywhere (poisson-disc.ts:152). Of 9119 seeds, 5102 fell outside the partitions (cellId -1, lines 139-143), because sampling covers [-100,500]² and the partitions only [0,400]². Those seeds are traced, lifted and given normals before visibility-cull drops them as off-mesh: wasted work. When densityScale < 1, keepProb exceeds 1, so the mechanism can never increase density.

sop/quadtree-root-bug.title: quadtree-subdivide starts from a max(w,h) square that spills past the canvas, and its output lacks the partition attributes
sop/quadtree-root-bug.evidence: cellSize = max(width, height) and cols = rows = ceil(w/cellSize) = 1 (lines 67-69), so the loop always runs once. In bun, an 800×400 input produced vertices up to y = 800. maxDepth is not rounded (line 36). It emits no cellId or depth attributes (lines 105-113), so poisson-disc's partition mode silently falls back when given its output (poisson-disc.ts:120-121). No patch uses this operator.
sop/quadtree-root-bug.recommendation: Tile with min(w,h) roots and clip. Share the leaf emitter with binary-subdivide so both emit cellId and depth. Add a test.
sop/quadtree-root-bug.verifyNote: In bun, 800×400 gives vertices up to y=800. Lines 67-69 compute cellSize = max(w,h), so there is a single root. maxDepth is not rounded (line 36), and no cellId or depth attributes are emitted. No patch uses the operator, but it is registered in allOperators and shown in the editor.

sop/merge-strip-and-dim-bugs.title: merge loses strips from inputs without stripOffsets and does not check dim or topology
sop/merge-strip-and-dim-bugs.evidence: stripOffsets are rebased only from inputs that have them (lines 91-96). An implicit single-strip input therefore gets no entry, and its vertices fold into nothing or into the previous strip; bun returned [2] for [implicit strip, explicit strip]. topology and dim are taken from geos[0] (lines 38-39) without checking the other inputs. attributes are dropped. When there is only one input it returns that same object (line 35); that is fine under immutability, but undocumented.

sop/param-validation.title: Param ranges are ignored and unvalidated, and some defaults sit outside their own ranges

- cook.ts:222-231 applies overrides raw.

In bun, poisson-disc with minRadius 0 throws a RangeError. parametric-surface with uSegments 4.5 gives vertexCount 27.5. cook.ts:222-231 applies params raw. Because collectParams uses the instance value as the slider default, the first slider touch in the inspector would snap Subscapes values into range and change the artwork.

sop/naming-vs-td.title: Several SOP names hide what they do or clash with TouchDesigner SOP names
sop/naming-vs-td.evidence:
The TouchDesigner names below are from my own knowledge (no web search was available).
- parametric-surface is a regular rows×cols grid, not a uv→xyz function; TD calls this the Grid SOP (rows/cols).
- continuous-stroke is a pass-through, i.e. a Null SOP.
- transform-2d corresponds to the Transform SOP, which is 3D.
- geometric-normal samples a field rather than the geometry; in TD, normals come from the Facet SOP or Attribute Create SOP and are computed from the mesh.
- 'subdivide' in binary-subdivide and quadtree-subdivide clashes with TD's Subdivide SOP, which is mesh smoothing; these are partitions.
- circle-pack does no circle packing; it is rejection-sampled scatter. TD's closest operator is the Sprinkle SOP.
- point-orient's docstring cites the Attribute Create SOP, but in TD that operator creates normals and tangents; custom per-point attributes come from the Point SOP.
- surface-raymarch is close to TD's Ray SOP.
- Param labels for one concept vary: 'Height', 'Height Scale', 'Terrain Amplitude', 'Displacement'.
sop/naming-vs-td.recommendation: Rename the misnamed ops, keep TD names where TD has the same operator, and use one label per concept.
sop/naming-vs-td.verifyNote: The code facts are right. parametric-surface is a rows×cols grid. continuous-stroke returns its input. transform-2d is 2D-only. circle-pack is dart-throwing rejection sampling with no radius variation. The label set is inconsistent: Height, Height Scale, Terrain Amplitude, Displacement. The TD equivalents named (Grid, Null, Transform, Facet / Attribute Create, Subdivide, Sprinkle, Point, Ray SOP) match my own knowledge.

sop/dead-and-redundant-sops.title: Dead barrel file, a no-op operator, a dominated duplicate, and attributes nobody reads
sop/dead-and-redundant-sops.evidence:
- sop/index.ts is imported by nothing (grep) and lacks surfaceLift and project3d, which a later commit added to operators/index.ts.
- continuous-stroke.ts:14-16 returns its input unchanged.
- circle-pack has the same params and output as poisson-disc, with fixed 3000 attempts at O(attempts×n) (lines 17-31, 51).
- surface-raymarch computes normalX/Y/Z (6 field evaluations per hit, lines 63-70, 130) and worldY, and nothing reads them; the only reference is the comment at types.ts:127.
- poisson-disc's cellId output has no consumer.
- visibility-cull's 'bypass' param (lines 39, 42-45) is a debug switch modelled as a slider; in TD, bypass is a flag every node has.
sop/dead-and-redundant-sops.recommendation: Delete sop/index.ts. Replace continuous-stroke with a generic null, or drop it from the patches. Fold circle-pack into poisson-disc and re-check flow-field. Compute attributes only on request. Make bypass a node-level kernel flag.
sop/dead-and-redundant-sops.verifyNote: grep finds no importer of sop/index.ts, and it lacks surfaceLift and project3d. continuous-stroke is a no-op but is used 7 times across the patches, so removing it means editing them. circle-pack is close to poisson-disc but not identical: it has no densityScale or partitions, its default minRadius is 50, and the flow-field patch uses it. Folding it in changes that patch's output. Nothing outside surface-raymarch reads normalX/Y/Z or worldY, and nothing reads cellId. bypass is a param slider (visibility-cull:39).

sop/flow-tracer-sampling.title: flow-tracer samples a discretised angle buffer by nearest neighbour with Euler steps, tying it to grid-sampler's layout
sop/flow-tracer-sampling.evidence: bufferAngle floors to a cell and reads data[col + row*width], ignoring channels (lines 7-11). It assumes channel 0 holds radians, which is grid-sampler's convention (grid-sampler.ts:42, 56). It needs width/height inputs only to recover the buffer's cell size (lines 35-36). Subscapes uses grid resolution 18px with an 8px step (subscapes-terrain-3d.ts:83, 101), so the angle is piecewise constant over about two steps, giving faceted streamlines.
sop/flow-tracer-sampling.recommendation: Accept a field or a vec2 buffer with bilinear sampling and RK2 integration. Store the cell size and origin in Buffer2D metadata.
sop/flow-tracer-sampling.verifyNote: bufferAngle floors and ignores channels (flow-tracer.ts:7-11), and integration is Euler. A related lookup bug is listed separately as a missed finding. grid-sampler samples at col·resolution, while flow-tracer maps with resX = width/buffer.width, so the two disagree.

sop/magic-constants.title: Behaviour-defining constants are hard-coded instead of exposed as params
sop/magic-constants.evidence:
- dash-stroke has no params; dashes are 2-7 vertices and gaps 1-5 vertices (lines 23-24), so dash length depends on the upstream step length.
- point-orient hard-codes aoFactor = 0.4 + 0.6a and a default depth of 0.5 (lines 65-68). Its noiseScale multiplies world coordinates (line 61) on top of the field's own noiseScale: Meridian applies 0.025 and 0.03 (meridian.ts:48, 81).
- poisson-disc fixes k = 30 (line 19), though the patch comment speaks of 'k=10 packing' (subscapes-terrain-3d.ts:96).
- circle-pack fixes 3000 attempts (line 51).
- visibility-cull offsets the ray origin by 0.01 (lines 292-294).
sop/magic-constants.recommendation: Expose arc-length dash and gap and k as params. Drop the double scaling. Expose the AO and depth blend factors.
sop/magic-constants.verifyNote: Each constant is as cited. Dash and gap lengths come from 2+floor(r·6) and 1+floor(r·5) (dash-stroke:23-24). point-orient hard-codes 0.4+0.6a and a depth default of 0.5 (lines 65-68), and its noiseScale multiplies on top of noiseAngle's 0.03; the actual lines are meridian.ts:49 and 82. Other constants: k=30 against the patch comment's k=10, 3000 attempts, and the 0.01 offset.

sop/cull-silent-passthrough.title: visibility-cull silently returns unculled geometry for points, implicit strips, or meshes without indices
sop/cull-silent-passthrough.evidence: visibility-cull.ts:47-50 returns the input unchanged when topology !== 'line-strip' or stripOffsets is missing. types.ts:113-118 says a missing stripOffsets is a valid single strip, so that geometry passes through. Lines 52-55 do the same for a non-indexed mesh. Any such input renders every hidden line, with no warning. No current patch feeds it such input, because pathsGeometry always sets stripOffsets.

sop/flow-grid-cell-mismatch.title: flow-tracer looks up the angle buffer with a different cell size than grid-sampler used to fill it
sop/flow-grid-cell-mismatch.evidence: grid-sampler sets cols = ceil(width/resolution) and samples the field at col·resolution (grid-sampler.ts:25, 56). flow-tracer maps a position to a cell using resX = width/buffer.width (flow-tracer.ts:35). With Subscapes (400 px, resolution 18) that gives 23 cols. Cells are sampled at x = 18·col but looked up over [17.39·col, 17.39·(col+1)), and the error grows to almost a full cell at the far edge.
sop/flow-grid-cell-mismatch.recommendation: Store the cell size and origin in Buffer2D metadata, written by grid-sampler, and use it in flow-tracer instead of re-deriving it from width and height.

mat-rop-chop/meridian-blank-at-size.title: Meridian renders blank above about 470 px: the scene-relative camera-3d is mixed with absolute raymarch distances

The comment at meridian.ts:52-54 shows the parameters were calibrated for sceneSize ≈ 256.

Add a headless bun regression test that cooks meridian at 256, 800 and 1600 with a stub createCanvas and asserts hits/seeds above a threshold, e.g. > 0.8, not just > 0.

mat-rop-chop/per-vertex-color-as-palette.title: Per-vertex colour is smuggled through the Palette type and detected by palette.count === vertexCount
mat-rop-chop/per-vertex-color-as-palette.evidence: diffuse-shade.ts:18-20 and :131 return {palette:{colors, count: vertexCount}}. stroke-renderer.ts:176 and :245 switch to per-vertex/per-strip colouring only when palette.count === vertexCount (plus stripOffsets); otherwise they silently use palette[0]. In subscapes-terrain-3d the 'palette' has 26,203 entries at 400 px (130,750 at 800 px) with only 5 unique colours. This sideband exists because project-3d.ts:46-54 drops normals and attributes, so colour cannot ride on the geometry. mat-rop-chop/camera3d-opaque-closures.title: Camera3D is opaque closures, so visibility-cull guesses the view direction from four hard-coded diagonals

mat-rop-chop/eager-readback-perf.title: Every rasteriser reads back all pixels to Float32 even when composite only uses the canvas, and the frame then throws the cache away

infra-history/wip-gpu-buffer-ownership.title: WIP GPU-resident buffers have contradictory ownership: blit frees textures the cache still holds, and replaced outputs leak
infra-history/wip-gpu-buffer-ownership.evidence:
Ownership is defined two incompatible ways:
- types.ts:181 says "Disposal happens via CookEngine.dispose()".
- canvas-2d.ts:142-157 renders the GPUBuffer2D, then calls `buffer.dispose()`, while the same object stays in CookEngine's cache.

Use after free: when the next draw finds nothing dirty (for example the ResizeObserver callback after the first draw, or the committed EditorPreview's persistent engine), findTerminalOutput returns the disposed buffer and blitTextureToCanvas binds a deleted texture. terrain-heightmap.ts:19 has field-render as its terminal, so that patch is exposed.

Leak: webgl.ts:330-346 renderFieldToTexture allocates a fresh texture and FBO on every call, and cook.ts:368 (and cook()) `cache.set` overwrites the old output without disposing it. Disposal happens only in dispose()/clearCache.

Smaller defects:
- TexturePool is exported but never used.
- types.ts:158 isGPUResident always returns true, even after dispose.
- types.ts:189 _readback ignores `channels` and always extracts the R channel.

These conclusions come from reading the code; nothing was run in a browser.
infra-history/wip-gpu-buffer-ownership.recommendation: Make CookEngine the sole owner of node outputs. It disposes a node's previous output when the node recooks, and on dispose/clearCache; blit and other consumers never dispose. Allocate through TexturePool, keyed per GL context. Add a bun:test with a fake GL that counts create and delete calls across cook, blit, re-blit and recook.
infra-history/wip-gpu-buffer-ownership.verifyNote:
In the main checkout:
- types.ts:181-183 (WIP) says disposal happens via CookEngine.dispose().
- The canvas-2d.ts blitBuffer2D GPU path calls `buffer.dispose()` after the blit, while the object stays in the cache.
- webgl.ts:330-371 renderFieldToTexture calls createTexture and createFramebuffer on every call.
- cook.ts:264 and :368 `cache.set` overwrite outputs without disposing them.
- texture-pool.ts is exported (render/index.ts:5) but used nowhere.
- isGPUResident returns `this.texture !== null`, which is always true.
Use-after-free path: in a frame, RAF callbacks run before ResizeObserver callbacks. So in the WIP Frame and in the committed EditorPreview (persistent engine, editor-preview.tsx:46-95), the initial RO callback triggers a second draw with nothing dirty. That draw returns the already-disposed terminal buffer, and terrain-heightmap's terminal is field-render. The `_readback ignores channels` point is moot: renderFieldToTexture always passes channels=1. Nothing was run in a browser.

Several operators draw from one stateful env.rng: circle-pack.ts:50, poisson-disc.ts:114, dash-stroke.ts:16, binary-subdivide.ts:54. env.rng is not a `$env` wire, so CookEngine's env diff never dirties on it.

On a partial recook, only the dirty nodes consume a fresh `new SeededRNG(...)`. Their random stream starts at the seed, whereas in a full cook it would start after upstream consumers' draws, so the output depends on edit history.

The committed EditorPreview already behaves this way: it keeps the engine across edits and builds `new SeededRNG(149149941)` per cook (editor-preview.tsx:62-68). Frame uses seed 42 (frame.tsx:141), so preview and frame differ anyway. The committed Frame hides the problem by calling `engine.clearCache()` after every draw (frame.tsx:163); the WIP removes that call.
infra-history/rng-partial-recook-nondete.recommendation: Derive a per-node RNG inside the cook from (graph seed, node key, optional node `seed` param). Remove rng from the shared env and remove the Math.random fallbacks. My own knowledge, unverified here, is that this matches TouchDesigner's per-operator Seed parameter. Use one seed source for Frame and EditorPreview, and add a test that a partial recook equals a full cook.
infra-history/rng-partial-recook-nondete.verifyNote: env.rng is consumed at circle-pack.ts:50, poisson-disc.ts:114, binary-subdivide.ts:54 and dash-stroke.ts:16, falling back to Math.random. GraphEnv.rng (types.ts:204) is not a `$env` wire, so the env diff in cook() never sees it. The committed EditorPreview keeps its engine across edits (only replaced when graph identity changes) and passes `new SeededRNG(149149941)` on each cook (editor-preview.tsx:62-68). Only dirty nodes then draw from a fresh stream, so the output depends on which nodes recooked. Frame uses seed 42 (frame.tsx:141), and the committed Frame masks the problem with clearCache() at :163, which the WIP removes.

infra-history/wip-cook-incremental-dupli.title: cookIncremental is a copy of cook() and mixes env snapshots across slices
infra-history/wip-cook-incremental-dupli.evidence:
- Duplication: cook.ts:296-395 re-implements cook()'s input gathering, variadic handling, param resolution and evaluate call line for line.
- Mixed env: the env diff runs only when a new incremental cook starts, but each later slice evaluates nodes with that call's `env` argument; `_incrEnv` is used only as an in-progress flag. A resize mid-cook therefore yields a cook that mixes two envs.
- Wasted work: `dirty` is cleared only at the end, so a restart after setParams recooks nodes that already finished.
- Finished and safe to port: the precomputed variadicPorts (constructor), `_buildParamIndex` (:475), and the topoSort queue head index replacing `queue.shift()` (graph.ts:136-138).
infra-history/wip-cook-incremental-dupli.recommendation: Extract a single `cookNode(key, env)`. Snapshot env once per cook and use the snapshot for every slice. Clear dirty per node in topological order; the propagate() early-exit at cook.ts:113-125 stays correct under that because dirty remains downward-closed. Port the three finished optimisations as separate small commits behind the restored meridian test.
infra-history/wip-cook-incremental-dupli.verifyNote:
- WIP cook.ts:296-395 repeats cook()'s input gathering, variadic handling, param resolution and evaluate call.
- The env diff runs only when `_incrEnv === null` (:299), but later slices evaluate with the `env` argument passed to that call (:368), so a resize mid-cook mixes envs. `_incrEnv` is used only as a flag.
- `dirty.clear()` runs only on completion, and setParams resets `_cursor = 0`, so nodes that already finished are recooked.
- The finished pieces are as described: variadicPorts in the constructor, `_buildParamIndex` at :475, and the topoSort head index at graph.ts:136-138.

infra-history/wip-stroke-lazy-readback-m.title: Lazy getImageData in stroke-renderer keeps every OffscreenCanvas alive, reversing a documented memory fix

infra-history/wip-stroke-lazy-readback-m.verifyNote: The WIP stroke-renderer canvasBuffer returns `get data()`, which closes over `canvas`. composite.ts:66 and :73 set `layers[i]._canvas = undefined` on the cached upstream outputs, but the closure keeps the OffscreenCanvas alive for as long as the output stays cached. infra-history/wip-field-jit.title: Field JIT looks finished and matches the interpreter, but has a cyclic import, possible exponential code size, and no test
infra-history/wip-field-jit.evidence:
Correctness: field-jit.ts:31-191 emits JS for every FieldExpr tag. Compared with evalExpr in field-expr.ts (div-by-zero → 0, pow with max(0,·), mix, smoothstep, fbm normalised by summed amplitude, warp offsets, apply), the semantics match. The WIP createField (field-expr.ts) tries the JIT and falls back to the interpreter on a CSP error.

Issues:
- field-expr.ts imports field-jit.ts and field-jit.ts imports FIELD_EXPR from field-expr.ts. This cycle is safe only because the function is called lazily.
- Both files import pnoise and simplex2 from operators/top, a kernel→operators dependency.
- Non-helper subexpressions are duplicated textually: `mix` emits `a` twice (:61-64), so nested or DAG-shaped expressions can grow the code exponentially.
- The code is recompiled with `new Function` on every createField, i.e. every cook.
- No test exists.
infra-history/wip-field-jit.recommendation:
Port it, with these changes:
1. Compile lazily on first invocation, which removes the cost on GPU-only chains.
2. Memoise helpers for any subexpression used twice, including mix and div operands.
3. Move FIELD_EXPR and the noise primitives into kernel modules to break the cycle and the kernel→operators edge.
4. Add a bun:test that compares JIT and interpreter output per tag at random (x,y).
infra-history/wip-field-jit.verifyNote:
The cycle is real: field-expr.ts imports jitCompileField, and field-jit.ts:3 imports the value FIELD_EXPR. It is safe only because the import is used lazily. Textual duplication occurs at :64 (`mix` emits `a` twice) and also at :53 (`div` emits the denominator twice), so nested mix/div grows the code exponentially and evaluates noise twice per pixel. fbm, warp and smoothstep correctly go through helpers.
One correction and one addition:
- The noise import from operators/top is not new; committed field-expr.ts:1-2 already has it.
- Every field operator (simplex, perlin, fbm, domain-warp, remap, curl, math, gradient) calls createField. Each node therefore recompiles its whole upstream subtree with `new Function`, which is O(N²) per full cook. On the GPU path that work is wasted, because field-render reads only FIELD_EXPR and never calls the JS function.

infra-history/wip-scheduler-fidelity.title: CookScheduler claims to mirror TouchDesigner, but the cook model is push-all-dirty and time-sliced, unlike TD's pull-based cooking
infra-history/wip-scheduler-fidelity.evidence: scheduler.ts:10-13 says "Mirrors TouchDesigner's cook loop". CookEngine cooks every dirty node in topological order, including nodes no viewer requests, and the WIP resumes partial cooks across frames. From my own knowledge (not verified here): TouchDesigner cooks on demand, pulling from what is viewed or output, so a dirty node cooks only when something downstream requests it. TD does not spread one network's cook over several frames; a heavy cook drops frames. The 60/40 budget split (scheduler.ts:96-103) also gives a lone engine only 60% of the budget.
infra-history/wip-scheduler-fidelity.recommendation: If fidelity is a goal, add `cook(requested)`, which walks upstream from requested terminals or viewers; that also serves editor node previews. Document time-slicing as a deliberate divergence, and give a lone engine the full budget.
infra-history/wip-scheduler-fidelity.verifyNote: scheduler.ts:10-13 claims to mirror TouchDesigner's cook loop. tick() at :83-111 gives index 0 `budgetMs * 0.6` even when it is the only cookable engine. CookEngine cooks every dirty node in order (cook.ts), not only requested outputs. The TouchDesigner side is from my own knowledge and not verifiable here: TD cooks on demand, pulled by viewers and outputs, and does not spread one network's cook across frames.

infra-history/wip-incremental-exception-.title: WIP cookIncremental advances the cursor before evaluate, so a throwing operator is skipped and then marked clean
infra-history/wip-incremental-exception-.evidence: In the WIP cookIncremental, `const key = this.order[this._cursor]!; this._cursor++;` runs before `op.evaluate(...)` at cook.ts:368, with no try/finally. If evaluate throws, `_incrEnv` stays non-null and the cursor already points past the failed node. The next draw() comes from the ResizeObserver or the next RAF; WIP frame.tsx:140-183 has no try/catch. That call resumes after the failed node, cooks its dependents with stale or undefined inputs, and on completion runs `this.dirty.clear()`, so the node is never retried until a param or env change. The committed cook() keeps the node dirty on a throw, so it retries on the next cook.
infra-history/wip-incremental-exception-.recommendation: Inside the shared cookNode, advance the cursor and clear the node's dirty flag only after evaluate succeeds. On a throw, reset the incremental state (or record the error per node, as TouchDesigner's per-operator error state does, from my knowledge) instead of resuming past it. Cover this in the cookNode unit test.

td-fidelity/taxonomy-cosmetic.title: Operator families are decorative and several operators sit in the wrong one
td-fidelity/taxonomy-cosmetic.evidence:
`category` (types.ts:12) only colours a dot in gen-node.tsx:15. Wire legality is PortType equality (graph.ts:85), with no family rule. Misassigned operators:
- camera-2d and camera-3d are category 'rop' (camera-2d.ts:14, camera-3d.ts:196) but are camera objects, which TD calls Camera COMPs.
- composite is 'rop' (composite.ts:36) but maps image to image (TD: Composite TOP).
- diffuse-shade is 'mat' (diffuse-shade.ts:30) but computes per-vertex colour and outputs a Palette.
- oklab-palette, procedural-palette and contrast-filter are 'mat' but produce colour lists; in TD that is CHOP or DAT data, while a MAT is a shader assigned at render.
'ROP' is Houdini's term; TD renders through a Render TOP. The TD statements are from my own knowledge.
td-fidelity/taxonomy-cosmetic.recommendation: Derive the family from PortType, so there is one source of truth: field→FIELD, image→TOP, geo2/geo3→SOP, channels→CHOP, camera→COMP. Drop the free-standing `category` field, or compute it from the operator's primary output. Move cameras to COMP and composite to TOP; turn renderers into TOPs; drop 'rop'. Keep wire legality as PortType equality and do not add a converter-port mechanism. Colour the editor by the derived family, which also fixes the missing 'rop' colour.
td-fidelity/taxonomy-cosmetic.verifyNote: Facts confirmed. category is read only by gen-node.tsx:15 for a dot colour, and CATEGORY_DOT (gen-node.tsx:5-11) has no 'rop' key, so every renderer, camera and composite falls back to the grey env colour. validateGraph checks only PortType equality (graph.ts:85). The family assignments are as stated: camera-2d.ts:14, camera-3d.ts:196 and composite.ts:36 are 'rop'; diffuse-shade.ts:30 and contrast-filter.ts:53 are 'mat' and output Palette. The TD statements (Camera COMP, Composite TOP, Render TOP, no ROP family in TD) match my own knowledge. Overstated in two ways. (1) A decorative label blocks nothing: wire legality already comes from PortType, which does the real work, so this is not 'high'. (2) The proposed converter/sampler-port rule duplicates what PortType equality already enforces; a second legality layer adds complexity for no gain.

td-fidelity/gpu-cpu-field-domain-mismatc.title: GPU and CPU paths sample fields in different coordinate domains and with different noise
td-fidelity/gpu-cpu-field-domain-mismatc.evidence:
Sampling coordinates:
- The compiled shader samples at `x = gl_FragCoord.x; y = uResolution.y - gl_FragCoord.y` (field-compiler.ts:391-392), with no pixel-to-world mapping.
- grid-sampler's CPU path samples at `col * resolution` (grid-sampler.ts:56), but its GPU path (taken when cols*rows > 500, l.30) samples at the grid index.
- In subscapes-terrain-3d (resolution 18, about 23×23 = 529 cells) the GPU path is taken, so the flow field's noiseScale, which was calibrated per pixel (patch comment l.66-69), is off by about 18×.
- field-render's CPU fallback divides by scale*dpr (field-render.ts:94-97); its GPU path ignores both.
Noise and precision:
- GLSL Perlin uses a sin-hash gradient (field-compiler.ts:31-51) while the CPU uses Perlin's permutation table.
- GLSL simplex scales by 130 (l.81) while the CPU scales by 70 (simplex-noise.ts:64).
- grid-sampler's GPU readback is 8-bit (webgl.ts:243-254).
The uncommitted grid-sampler change in the main checkout does not fix any of this.
td-fidelity/gpu-cpu-field-domain-mismatc.recommendation: As proposed: give rasterising TOPs an explicit world domain and pass it as a uDomain uniform (also correcting the +0.5 pixel-centre offset), and use one noise implementation in both interpreters. Add a bun test that compares evalExpr against expected values for each FieldExpr tag. Because the GLSL side cannot run headless, also add a browser check that renders one patch on both paths and diffs them.
td-fidelity/gpu-cpu-field-domain-mismatc.verifyNote:
Domain mismatch:
- The compiled shader uses x = gl_FragCoord.x and y = uResolution.y - gl_FragCoord.y (field-compiler.ts main, lines ~391-392). That is pixel centres (+0.5) in buffer pixels.
- grid-sampler's GPU branch renders a cols×rows target (grid-sampler.ts:34-38), so it samples at grid indices; its CPU branch samples at col*resolution (l.56).
- field-render's CPU branch divides by scale*dpr (l.94-97); its GPU branch does not. So on a dpr-2 display every GPU field-render shows 2× the noise features of the same patch at dpr 1.
Noise mismatch:
- GLSL Perlin uses the sin hash (field-compiler.ts:31-51); CPU Perlin uses the permutation table.
- GLSL simplex is the Ashima variant ×130 (l.81); CPU simplex is ×70 with a different gradient set (simplex-noise.ts:11-14, 64).
- renderFieldToBuffer reads back UNSIGNED_BYTE (webgl.ts:243-254), which quantises and clamps to [0,1].
Which path runs depends on the viewport. GPU is used only when cols*rows > 500, i.e. square side > 396 px at resolution 18. The lg gallery card is about 395 px → 22×22 = 484 → CPU path; md and mobile cards are larger → GPU path. So the subscapes flow field switches between two different images at layout breakpoints. On the GPU path, noiseScale 0.00025 × ~23 cells is essentially a constant angle.
The uncommitted grid-sampler diff in the main checkout only changes where the GL context comes from.

td-fidelity/palette-overloaded.title: Palette means three different things and consumers guess which
td-fidelity/palette-overloaded.recommendation: As proposed: per-vertex colour becomes a Cd attribute on geometry. Shading becomes a SOP that writes Cd. A palette-lookup SOP maps a scalar attribute through a palette into Cd. A palette is a typed colour table (CHOP-like channels), and renderers read colour only from Cd or a single colour parameter.

td-fidelity/field-algebra-gaps.title: Field algebra lacks constants and domain/value transforms, so scale knobs leak into consumers
td-fidelity/field-algebra-gaps.recommendation: Make fbm emit apply(...) for domainRotation instead of a closure. Add a `field-transform` operator built on the existing `apply` plus mul/add (domain translate/rotate/scale, value gain/offset); no new FieldExpr tag is needed. Add a `constant` field operator over c()/u(). Then remove amplitude/baseY from the SOPs and the scale knobs from curl-noise and point-orient.

td-fidelity/geometry-dim-untyped.title: 2D and 3D geometry share one port type; merge and transform-2d corrupt mixed input
td-fidelity/geometry-dim-untyped.evidence: PortType has a single 'geometry' (types.ts:28) for Geometry<2> and Geometry<3>. validateGraph therefore accepts a 2D input to project-3d, which reads `src[i*3..i*3+2]` (project-3d.ts:37-39), or a 3D input to surface-lift. merge takes dim and topology from the first input (merge.ts:38-39) and copies `g.vertexCount * dim` floats from every input (l.66-68), so mixing 2D and 3D corrupts positions; commit 2b7e755 claims merge was 'generalized to support mixed 2D/3D geometry'. merge also mixes topologies silently. transform-2d allocates a full-length output but writes only x and y (transform-2d.ts:34-46), which zeroes Z on 3D input.
td-fidelity/geometry-dim-untyped.recommendation: Split the port type into geo2/geo3, or carry dim in PortDef and check it in validateGraph. merge must reject mismatched dim/topology and must synthesise a strip offset for inputs without stripOffsets. Replace transform-2d with a transform SOP that copies the remaining components.
td-fidelity/geometry-dim-untyped.verifyNote:
There is one 'geometry' PortType for Geometry<2> and Geometry<3> (types.ts:28).
- project-3d reads src[i*3..i*3+2] (l.37-39).
- surface-lift reads src[i*2] (l.45-46).
- merge takes topology and dim from geos[0] (l.38-39) and copies g.vertexCount*dim floats per input (l.66-68), so mixed dims corrupt positions. Commit 2b7e755's message does claim 'Merge generalized to support mixed 2D/3D geometry'.
- merge also loses strip boundaries when an input has no stripOffsets: its vertices are appended to the previous strip.

td-fidelity/camera-opaque-closure.title: Camera3D is a pair of opaque closures; visibility-cull has to guess the eye direction
td-fidelity/camera-opaque-closure.evidence: Camera3D is {project, unproject, viewport} (types.ts:179-192), with no eye, forward or matrices, so it cannot be inspected or serialised. visibility-cull finds the camera direction by probing project() at 4 fixed diagonal directions (visibility-cull.ts:254-275). That only works for orthographic cameras in those octants, although the docstring (l.25-26) claims it is general-purpose. visibility-cull also infers the grid size from `meshIdx[2]` on the assumption that the mesh came from parametric-surface (l.125-131). camera-3d's fallbacks `eyeX ?? 300`, `eyeY ?? 400`, `orthoSize ?? 500` (l.246-264) are stale absolute units, against defaults of 0.75, 1.0 and 1.25 (l.216-224).
td-fidelity/camera-opaque-closure.recommendation: As proposed: make Camera3D plain data {view, proj, viewProj, invViewProj, eye, forward, viewport} with project/unproject as kernel functions. visibility-cull should use camera.forward (or a per-point view ray for perspective) and take the mesh grid size explicitly or use a spatial index.

Confirmed:

td-fidelity/grid-sampler-gl-context-leak.title: grid-sampler creates a new WebGL2 context on every GPU evaluation
td-fidelity/grid-sampler-gl-context-leak.evidence: When cols*rows > 500, grid-sampler calls env.createCanvas(cols, rows) and then createWebGL2(canvas) inside evaluate (grid-sampler.ts:32-35), ignoring the env._gl that Frame provides (frame.tsx:142) and that field-render uses (field-render.ts:18-29). Frame calls engine.clearCache() after every draw (frame.tsx:163), so every resize or parameter change re-cooks grid-sampler and creates another context. The compiled-program cache is per context, so the shader is also recompiled each time. Browsers cap live WebGL contexts and drop the oldest when the cap is exceeded (my own knowledge, about 16 in Chrome); the dropped one can be the shared context every Frame's field-render uses (frame.tsx:14-23). field-render would then fall to its CPU path, which samples a different domain (see gpu-cpu-field-domain-mismatch). The uncommitted grid-sampler diff in the main checkout fixes exactly this ('Avoids creating a new WebGL context per evaluation').
td-fidelity/grid-sampler-gl-context-leak.recommendation: Use env._gl in grid-sampler, as field-render does (or take the main-checkout change when it lands). Longer term, give cook a single GPU capability object instead of letting operators create contexts.

td-fidelity/stroke-renderer-eager-readba.title: Every stroke-renderer does a full-frame float readback that only the CPU composite fallback uses, and still keeps the canvas alive
td-fidelity/stroke-renderer-eager-readba.evidence: canvasBuffer (stroke-renderer.ts:355-367) calls getImageData and converts every byte into a Float32Array on every render, and also attaches `_canvas`. The doc comment claims the eager readback lets the canvas be freed, but the cached output keeps referencing the canvas through `_canvas` until composite mutates it away. The data is used only when composite takes its CPU fallback. At 800×800 CSS px and dpr 2, one render is 1600×1600×4 floats (about 41 MB); subscapes has three renderers, about 120 MB per draw. That matches the '~100 MB per panel' comment that motivated clearing the whole cache after every draw (frame.tsx:159-163). composite's canvas path already uses a lazy `data` getter (composite.ts:79-90).
td-fidelity/stroke-renderer-eager-readba.recommendation: Make stroke-renderer's `data` lazy, as composite's is, or better, return a canvas/texture-backed Image and read back only on demand. This would also let Frame keep its cache and benefit from incremental cooking.

td-fidelity/patch-params-outside-declare.title: Patches set parameter values outside the operators' declared ranges, so the inspector cannot represent them
td-fidelity/patch-params-outside-declare.recommendation: Add a registration and validateGraph check that every default and every instance param is within [min, max]. Fix the ranges, which ideally become world-unit ranges once units are resolution-independent.

td-fidelity/geometric-normal-boundary-fl.title: geometric-normal inverts the normal wherever only one axis falls back to a forward difference
td-fidelity/geometric-normal-boundary-fl.evidence: geometric-normal.ts:60-89 uses tx = -eps (backward) when px ≥ eps and tx = +eps (forward) otherwise, and the same for uz on Z. The cross product's y component is ny = uz*tx - ux*tz = uz*tx. On flat ground ny is +eps² when both axes use the same branch and -eps² when they differ. So any vertex with exactly one of x or z below eps gets a downward normal, which flips its Lambert shading in diffuse-shade and its back-face result in visibility-cull. flow-tracer lets strokes run to -exitMargin (flow-tracer.ts:58-61), so negative-coordinate vertices in the margin take the forward branch on one axis and hit this case.
td-fidelity/geometric-normal-boundary-fl.recommendation: Use central differences on both axes, as field-gradient does, or keep the tangent sign consistent. Better, derive N from the field-gradient dx/dy fields so there is one gradient implementation.
